Questions

## Frequently asked questions

How does StackSnap calculate the savings counter?

Four categories of avoided cost:

- Duplicate ingredients — two supplements containing overlapping active ingredients (your multivitamin has magnesium and you also take a separate magnesium glycinate)

- Potential overdoses — amounts above tolerable upper intake levels (16,000% RDA of B12 across your B-complex plus a separate B12 sublingual)

- Low-quality brand premium — where you pay significantly above U.S. median for the same ingredient

- Supplements with no published evidence for the stated benefit

The dollar number reflects what the average user could redirect by acting on findings. Actual savings depend on which supplements you choose to discontinue or replace — StackSnap shows the information, you make the call.

How accurate is the drug interaction checker?

StackSnap uses RxNav — the National Library of Medicine's drug interaction reference database. Same dataset pharmacists consult.

Interactions are based on documented mechanisms: cytochrome P450 effects (drugs metabolized through liver enzymes), absorption competition (iron vs calcium), blood-thinning additivity (fish oil + warfarin), blood-pressure compounding (potassium + ACE inhibitors), etc.

This is a screening tool, not a medical diagnosis. Always confirm any flagged interaction with your pharmacist or doctor before changing any supplement or medication.

What is the NIH DSLD database?

The NIH Dietary Supplement Label Database (DSLD) is a U.S. National Institutes of Health database indexing over 130,000 supplement product labels with verified ingredient amounts and source citations.

StackSnap pulls scan results directly from DSLD rather than using proprietary "TrustScore" systems that change without explanation. Every ingredient you see has a documented government-database source — verifiable in the public NIH database.

Is StackSnap a medical device or does it give medical advice?

No. StackSnap is a general wellness app designed to help organize and understand your supplement routine. It is not a medical device, is not FDA-cleared as such, and does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment recommendations.

Always consult a qualified healthcare professional — your doctor, pharmacist, or registered dietitian — before starting, stopping, or changing any supplement or medication. Do not disregard professional medical advice based on information from this app.

Will StackSnap diagnose what I should take?

No. StackSnap is an organizational and informational tool, not a recommendation engine.

It tells you what you are taking, what overlaps exist, what amounts are above standard upper intake levels, and what interactions might exist with your prescriptions. It does not tell you what you should take — that's a decision to make with your doctor or registered dietitian.

What supplement categories does StackSnap work on?

Broadly: anything indexed in NIH DSLD.

- Vitamins — A, B-complex (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9, B12), C, D, E, K

- Minerals — calcium, magnesium, zinc, iron, selenium, chromium, iodine, potassium

- Amino acids — L-theanine, glutamine, taurine, BCAAs, lysine, tryptophan

- Herbals — turmeric, ashwagandha, ginkgo, milk thistle, rhodiola, ginger

- Nootropics — Alpha-GPC, Lion's Mane, Bacopa, Phosphatidylserine, Citicoline

- Other — omega-3s, probiotics, protein powders, pre-workout supplements, sleep aids (melatonin, valerian, L-tryptophan), adaptogens

Does StackSnap have a drug interaction database for prescriptions?

Yes. RxNav covers FDA-approved prescription medications and their documented interactions with supplements and other drugs.

Add your prescriptions once (input by drug name or scan the prescription label), and StackSnap automatically cross-references them whenever you scan a new supplement.

What is the doctor PDF and when should I use it?

A clean 1-page PDF summary of every supplement in your stack: brand, ingredient, daily amount, timing, any flagged interactions or potential overdoses.

Use before any healthcare provider visit:

- Primary care annual exams

- Endocrinologist visits

- Pharmacist consultations

- Naturopath sessions

- Pre-op consultations (some supplements affect bleeding and anesthesia)

Saves 5–10 minutes of fumbling through bottles and gives your provider real information to work from.

Can StackSnap remind me when to take each supplement?

Yes. Smart reminders organize by recommended timing:

- Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) — with the largest meal

- Magnesium glycinate — at night for sleep support

- B-complex — morning, away from caffeine

- Berberine — with carb-heavy meals

- Melatonin — 30 minutes before sleep

- Iron — away from coffee and dairy

All reminders are customizable. You can set per-supplement schedules.

What is the difference between weekly and annual subscription?

Identical features. Weekly is $4.99/week (best for short-term tracking during a new health protocol or supplement experiment). Annual is $39.99/year (saves over 84% vs weekly). For most users who scan their stack once or twice a month and review interactions periodically, annual is the better economic choice — most users identify more than $39.99 in savings in the first month alone.

How do I cancel StackSnap Pro?

All subscriptions managed through Apple. To cancel:

- Open Settings

- Tap your Apple ID at the top

- Tap Subscriptions

- Find StackSnap → tap Cancel Subscription

Takes effect at end of current billing period. The 7-day trial can be cancelled any time before it ends with no charge.

Where does my data go? Is it private?

StackSnap uses SwiftData local-first storage — your supplement stack data is stored on your iPhone first, with iCloud sync optional.

Anonymous scan metadata may be used to improve the AI model. Health-related data is never shared with third parties or used for advertising. Full privacy policy: love8ko.github.io/stacksnap/privacy-policy.html.

Will I lose my stack data if I cancel?

No. Your scanned stack data persists locally on the device even after cancellation or sign-out (unlike Care/of, Prove It, and similar apps that wipe the stack on logout).

You retain read access to historical scans, the doctor PDF feature, and your stack list — but lose access to new scans, the interaction checker, and ongoing reminders unless you resubscribe.

Does StackSnap track supplements I bought from non-US brands?

Coverage is strongest for U.S.-marketed brands indexed by NIH DSLD. For European, Australian, or Asian brands not in DSLD, you can manually enter the ingredient list and StackSnap will check it against the same overlap and interaction logic.

The NIH database keeps growing — coverage improves over time.

Can StackSnap detect counterfeit or fake supplements?

No. Counterfeit detection requires lab testing of the contents. StackSnap reads the label and the database entry, not the actual substance in the bottle.

For verifying authenticity of expensive or rare supplements, third-party testing (LabDoor, ConsumerLab) is necessary. StackSnap can flag suspicious patterns (unusually low price for a high-end ingredient, unlisted manufacturer) but cannot confirm or rule out counterfeits.

Is StackSnap suitable for tracking my child's supplements?

StackSnap is designed for adult supplement tracking. Pediatric dosing has different upper intake limits, age-specific interaction profiles, and considerations that StackSnap is not specifically calibrated for.

The doctor PDF feature still works for organizing the list for pediatric visits — but always consult a pediatrician for dosing or interaction questions specific to children.

Does StackSnap work with HealthKit?

Yes. StackSnap integrates with Apple HealthKit so your supplement schedule and adherence can sit alongside your other health data (workouts, sleep, prescriptions). HealthKit integration is optional and can be enabled or disabled in Settings.

What happens if StackSnap flags an interaction with my medication?

You see an alert with:

- Specific mechanism — e.g. "St. John's Wort accelerates the metabolism of many medications via CYP3A4 induction, potentially reducing efficacy"

- Severity classification — theoretical, mild, moderate, severe

- Recommendation — consult your pharmacist or doctor before making any changes

Never stop a prescribed medication based on a StackSnap flag — always speak to your prescribing physician first. The flag is the AI noticing a documented risk; the clinical judgment about what to do is your healthcare provider's.

How does StackSnap compare to SuppCo and Prove It?

SuppCo (18,780 App Store reviews) shows proprietary TrustScores that fluctuate without explanation. StackSnap shows you dollar-savings from your specific stack plus the underlying ingredient data sourced directly to NIH DSLD entries.

Prove It (13,842 reviews) is currently struggling with 83% of recent reviews rating 1 star — primarily due to dark-pattern paywall complaints and absence of a real free trial.

StackSnap is built specifically as the honest alternative: full Pro access during the 7-day trial, no quiz, transparent pricing, RxNav interaction checks, doctor PDF export.

7-day free trial with full Pro access. No 20-question quiz before you see the app, no email signup gate, no credit card required upfront.

- Weekly: $4.99/week

Editorial · 2026 Ranking

# The best supplement tracker apps of 2026, ranked.

Five iOS apps worth considering, ranked by data transparency, drug interaction checking, and honest pricing — with honest trade-offs for each.

 See the ranking

Context

## The state of supplement trackers in 2026

77% of American adults take supplements. Five iOS apps in 2026 are worth considering.

The category has been plagued by dark-pattern paywalls (Prove It currently has 83% 1-star reviews on recent submissions) and opaque proprietary scoring systems. The ranking below weights transparency, drug interaction checking, and honest pricing heavily.

### What no supplement tracker app can do (yet)

- Provide medical advice — all apps are general wellness tools, none are medical devices. Always consult a healthcare professional for decisions.

- Detect counterfeit supplements — requires lab testing of contents. Apps read labels, not what's actually in the bottle.

- Predict individual responses — supplements work differently in different bodies based on genetics, gut microbiome, existing nutritional status, and prescriptions. No app can predict your individual response.

- Replace pharmacist clinical judgment — interaction flags are screening tools; final clinical decisions require a pharmacist or doctor.

### The recommendation

For most supplement users in 2026:

- If you take any prescription medication, StackSnap is the only choice with drug interaction checking — the safety value alone justifies it.

- If you take no prescriptions and just want supplement tracking with a big review base, SuppCo works fine — pay the price premium for established polish.

- If you're currently using Prove It and frustrated, StackSnap was built specifically for the migration — honest 7-day trial, no quiz, transparent pricing.

Download StackSnap for the 7-day free trial. Scan your shelf in 20 minutes. If it finds at least one duplicate or one interaction you didn't know about, the value is proven. If not, cancel before the trial ends.

Overview

## What is Folik?

Folik is an educational companion app for adults experiencing hair thinning, hair loss, or pattern hair loss who want a tracking tool with cited sources instead of marketing language.

It is not a medical device. It does not prescribe finasteride, dutasteride, minoxidil, or any medication. It does not diagnose alopecia areata, scarring alopecia, or any condition. It is a tracker plus a research-grounded reference layer that sits between dermatology visits, so the conversation with your dermatologist is more productive — not replaced.

What it is not: Folik is not a hair growth supplement promoter, a transplant clinic referral service, a telehealth pharmacy, or a snake-oil store. The AI Coach is grounded in AAD, ISHRS, FDA, and PubMed sources — not influencer recommendations or affiliate-loaded hot takes. The Coach does not push you toward or away from any treatment.

The sources Folik surfaces: American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) publicly available position statements and treatment guidelines; International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery (ISHRS) publicly available resources; FDA prescribing information for finasteride, minoxidil, and related medications, plus public safety communications; and 50+ peer-reviewed PubMed studies including Blume-Peytavi et al. 2011, Kaufman et al. 1998, Dhurat et al. 2013, and Avci et al. 2014. Folik is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the AAD, ISHRS, or FDA.

Audience

## Who Folik is built for

### Men noticing early recession or crown thinning

The earliest months of pattern hair loss are where the most action lives. Free Norwood calculator gives you a starting reference point. The Coach answers "is this really happening?" with cited sources. The photo journal starts the longitudinal record that will matter at month 12.

### Already on finasteride and/or minoxidil

Without calibrated photos and a fixed staging method, "is it working" is a feeling not a fact. Ghost overlay + pixel-density measurement give you evidence. The treatment tracker correlates with the photo journal so you can see whether week 16 actually looks different from week 4.

### Women with diffuse thinning or widening part

Ludwig staging, AAD female pattern hair loss resources, and explicit Coach guidance on what finasteride/dutasteride are NOT appropriate for (women of childbearing potential — FDA Pregnancy Category X). For postpartum telogen effluvium, the Coach surfaces that this often resolves on its own and recommends dermatology evaluation.

### Considering finasteride, concerned about side effects

The Coach surfaces the published evidence on post-finasteride syndrome, the prevalence of reported sexual side effects in clinical trials and post-marketing reports, the persistence concerns, and the structured questions to bring to your dermatologist before starting — including baseline sexual function documentation and informed consent.

### Post-transplant, tracking graft growth

ISHRS guidelines on post-transplant care, expected timeline (initial shock loss, then growth phases at months 4–12), and what photos to bring to follow-up visits. Folik is not a transplant clinic referral service — no commercial relationship with any clinic.

### Privacy-conscious users

Hair loss photos are sensitive. All photos and tracking data stay on your device. No account required for the free Norwood calculator. Premium subscription is App-Store-managed and does not require name, email, or any identity disclosure to Folik directly.

Capabilities

## Six things Folik does that other hair loss apps don't

- AI Hair Loss Coach with cited sources on every reply. Ask anything — "Will minoxidil cause initial shedding?" "Is post-finasteride syndrome real?" "Is dutasteride approved for hair loss?" Every reply cites the underlying source: AAD treatment guideline section, ISHRS resource, FDA prescribing information document, or specific PubMed study with year and authors. The Coach does not prescribe, diagnose, or recommend dose changes.

- Free Norwood and Ludwig Calculator — no signup, no paywall. Open the app, take or upload a photo, get your Norwood stage (men, stages I–VII including Vertex variant) or Ludwig stage (women, stages I–III) in 30 seconds. Most competitor apps lock staging behind a subscription wall; Folik locks the interpretation, not the result.

- Calibrated 5-angle photo journal with ghost overlay alignment. Repeatable photos are the single most useful self-tracking habit in hair loss. Ghost overlay alignment means the previous scan ghosts into your viewfinder so you frame the new one identically. Five angles per scan: hairline, crown, front part, left temple, right temple. Pixel-density measurement on the same anatomical region across scans — evidence you can actually trust.

- Treatment tracker with side-effect logging. Log topical minoxidil (2% or 5%), oral minoxidil, finasteride (1mg and 5mg), dutasteride, microneedling sessions, supplements (biotin, vitamin D, zinc, saw palmetto), ketoconazole shampoo, and LLLT. Track adherence. Log side effects with a structured form and timeline — useful for the dermatology appointment.

- Norwood/Ludwig AI visual analysis with 90-day restaging. Beyond the one-shot calculator, Folik can re-stage you over time. Stage IIA progressing toward Stage III in 90 days is meaningful information. Stable Stage III for 12 months on finasteride suggests the treatment is holding. Staging is consistent across scans because the framing is calibrated.

- Explicit off-label and safety disclosures. Dutasteride for hair loss is off-label in the US. Oral minoxidil for hair loss is off-label. Finasteride and dutasteride are FDA Pregnancy Category X — not appropriate for women of childbearing potential. Post-finasteride syndrome reports are cited honestly, not dismissed. Folik surfaces these on every relevant Coach reply.

Workflow

## How to track hair loss treatment progress — a 12-month framework

This is the practical workflow Folik is built around, based on AAD guidelines, FDA prescribing information, and published clinical trials.

- Day 0 — establish your calibrated baseline.Before starting any treatment, take five calibrated angles (hairline, crown, front part, left temple, right temple) under consistent lighting. Note your starting Norwood/Ludwig stage. The free calculator gives you this in 30 seconds. Save context labs if available (testosterone, SHBG, iron/ferritin, thyroid) for later correlation. Without this baseline, you will spend month 6 trying to remember what your hairline looked like in January. You will not remember.

- Months 1–3 — expect shedding, not visible growth.This is where most people quit. Minoxidil-induced shedding peaks weeks 2–8 — it is a documented sign the medication is activating follicles, not a sign of failure (Blume-Peytavi et al. 2011; FDA Rogaine® prescribing information). Finasteride works at the DHT level; visible results lag by 3–6 months minimum. Kaufman et al. 1998 showed first measurable density change around month 6. Log side effects carefully — sexual side effects on finasteride warrant immediate contact with your prescriber. Take monthly photos with ghost overlay alignment.

- Months 3–6 — stabilization phase.Most users report a noticeable decrease in shedding by month 4. Density change is still mostly invisible to the naked eye but pixel-density measurement may show early movement. The crown responds first; the frontal hairline responds last and least to finasteride — a well-documented clinical reality. Treatment adherence is the single biggest variable in 12-month outcomes; track it honestly in the treatment log.

- Months 6–12 — first meaningful comparison.Pull up your day-zero baseline. Compare the same five calibrated angles at month 6 and month 12 with the side-by-side slider. Most users on combined minoxidil + finasteride show measurable improvement by month 12 in the crown and mid-scalp per published trials. Stabilization (stopping progression) is a successful outcome — the AAD guidelines frame holding the line as a primary treatment goal, not just regrowth. Continued visible thinning after 12 months of consistent use warrants dermatology re-evaluation.

- Month 12 — dermatology check-in with evidence.Bring the photo journal (all five angles at day 0, months 3, 6, 9, 12), the treatment adherence log, and the side-effect log. Ask: "Is this trajectory in line with what you expect?" "If we wanted to escalate, what would you consider?" "What labs are worth running annually on this protocol?" Specific documented questions get specific answers. The 12 months of calibrated tracking justify this appointment.

In the wild

## Real scenarios where Folik earns its keep

### First three months — the shedding panic

Marcus started finasteride + topical minoxidil six weeks ago. His shedding has increased. He opens the AI Coach and asks "is this normal?" The Coach replies with the FDA Rogaine® prescribing information explanation of telogen effluvium, the Blume-Peytavi et al. 2011 shedding timeline, and the Kaufman et al. 1998 note that visible density change typically starts around month 6. Source cited. Marcus does not quit at week 6. At month 12 his crown photos show meaningful stabilization.

### Considering finasteride — the PFS question

David has read about post-finasteride syndrome online and is concerned. He asks the Folik Coach: "Is PFS real?" The Coach surfaces the FDA-required label warnings on sexual side effects, the published post-marketing case series on persistence concerns, and the recommendation to document baseline sexual function before starting and discuss this explicitly with his prescriber for informed consent. Not minimized, not catastrophized — cited evidence. David goes to his dermatologist with specific questions.

### Dutasteride — the off-label question

Sarah's dermatologist has suggested dutasteride for her pattern hair loss. She asks Folik: "Is dutasteride approved for hair loss?" The Coach replies: FDA-approved for BPH only in the US; off-label for hair loss in the US; approved for hair loss in South Korea and Japan. Inhibits both type I and type II 5α-reductase isoenzymes — stronger DHT suppression than finasteride, stronger side-effect profile. FDA Pregnancy Category X — Sarah notes that since she is not of childbearing potential, this does not apply, but the Coach surfaces it anyway for completeness. She returns to her dermatologist with an informed question list.

### 12-month dermatology visit

Nina has been using Folik for a year. She brings the 12-month calibrated photo journal to her appointment — all five angles at day 0, months 3, 6, 9, and 12. The ghost overlay alignment means the dermatologist can see that the photos are actually comparable. The pixel-density chart shows a 12% improvement in crown density. The treatment adherence log shows 94% minoxidil adherence and 89% finasteride adherence. The side-effect log shows two weeks of scalp irritation at month 2 that resolved. This is a productive appointment.

### Post-transplant monitoring

James had an FUE hair transplant in January. He uses Folik to track the post-transplant timeline: initial shock loss (weeks 2–6), follicular recovery (weeks 6–12), early regrowth (months 3–6), full results (months 9–12 per ISHRS guidelines). Ghost overlay alignment means his monthly crown photos are calibrated to the same angle, so the graft growth evidence is real, not just better lighting this month.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Who is Folik built for?

Adults — men and women — experiencing hair thinning, hair loss, or pattern hair loss who want a tracking tool grounded in published evidence rather than marketing language. Common users include men in their 20s through 50s noticing recession or crown thinning, women dealing with diffuse thinning or postpartum recovery, patients already on finasteride or minoxidil tracking results, and post-transplant patients monitoring graft growth. Not for diagnosing alopecia areata, scarring alopecia, or any clinical condition — that requires a dermatologist.

What does Folik actually do?

Folik is an educational hair loss companion app. It combines an AI Hair Loss Coach trained on publicly available AAD, ISHRS, FDA, and 50+ peer-reviewed PubMed studies with a calibrated photo journal that uses ghost overlay alignment for repeatable framing and pixel-density measurement for real progress detection. The free Norwood/Ludwig calculator works without signup. Folik does not prescribe medication, diagnose conditions, or replace consultation with a dermatologist.

Is Folik a medical device?

No. Folik is an educational companion app. It does not prescribe finasteride, dutasteride, minoxidil, or any medication. It does not diagnose hair loss type. It does not replace consultation with a dermatologist. It surfaces publicly available evidence from AAD, ISHRS, FDA, and 50+ peer-reviewed PubMed studies, and tracks treatments you are already using under medical guidance.

Is the Norwood calculator really free with no signup?

Yes. Open the app, take or upload a photo, get your Norwood (for men) or Ludwig (for women) stage in roughly 30 seconds. No account creation, no email, no subscription required. The AI Coach interpretation of your stage requires the Premium subscription, but the staging result itself is permanently free.

What sources does the AI Hair Loss Coach actually cite?

Every Coach reply cites the underlying source: AAD (American Academy of Dermatology) publicly available position statements and treatment guidelines for androgenetic alopecia; ISHRS (International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery) publicly available resources on transplant outcomes and standards; FDA prescribing information for finasteride, minoxidil, and related medications, plus FDA public safety communications; and 50+ peer-reviewed PubMed studies including Blume-Peytavi et al. 2011 (minoxidil density), Kaufman et al. 1998 (finasteride DHT mechanism), Dhurat et al. 2013 (microneedling-minoxidil synergy), Avci et al. 2014 (low-level laser therapy).

How does the photo journal work?

Five-angle guided capture: hairline, crown, front part, left temple, right temple. Each new scan uses ghost overlay alignment — the previous scan ghosts into your viewfinder so you frame the new photo identically. This is the single most important feature for trustworthy progress tracking because most apparent progress in non-calibrated photos is just lighting or angle change. Pixel-density measurement on the same anatomical region across scans gives a quantitative track. Side-by-side comparison slider between any two scans. All photos stay local on your device.

How is Folik different from Regrow Hair AI or other hair loss apps?

Most hair loss apps give you a generic hair score (7.2 out of 10) without showing the math. Folik shows the sources. Every AI Coach reply cites the underlying AAD guideline, ISHRS resource, FDA prescribing information document, or peer-reviewed PubMed study. The photo journal uses ghost overlay alignment and pixel-density measurement instead of vague visual scoring. The Norwood calculator is free with no signup, which most competitor apps lock behind subscriptions. Regrow Hair AI is the more established #1 app with a larger installed base and polished UX — pick Folik if cited sources matter most to you; pick Regrow if you want the most mature product.

Will the Coach tell me to start finasteride?

No. The Coach surfaces what AAD guidelines, FDA prescribing information, and peer-reviewed studies say about finasteride — mechanism (5α-reductase inhibition, DHT reduction), efficacy in clinical trials (Kaufman et al. 1998), known side-effect profile, and post-marketing reports including post-finasteride syndrome. The decision to start finasteride is between you and a dermatologist who can evaluate your full picture (medical history, baseline sexual function, family history, alternatives). We do not recommend treatments.

What does the Coach say about post-finasteride syndrome (PFS)?

The Coach surfaces the published evidence honestly. PFS is reported in the medical literature with persistence concerns. It is also a contested clinical area where some dermatologists minimize the reports and others take them seriously. The Coach does not dismiss the reports nor pretend they don't exist. It cites the FDA-required label warnings, the published post-marketing case series, and recommends that anyone considering finasteride discuss this with their dermatologist before starting — including documenting baseline sexual function and informed consent.

Is dutasteride approved for hair loss in the US?

No. Dutasteride (Avodart®, GlaxoSmithKline) is FDA-approved in the US for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) only. Use for hair loss is off-label in the US. It is approved for hair loss in some other countries including South Korea and Japan. Dutasteride is a more complete 5α-reductase inhibitor than finasteride (inhibits both type I and type II isoenzymes) which can produce stronger results but also stronger side-effect risk. If your dermatologist prescribes dutasteride for hair loss, that is a clinical decision under their professional judgment. The Coach surfaces the off-label status explicitly so you can have an informed conversation.

What about oral minoxidil for hair loss?

Oral minoxidil is FDA-approved for treatment-resistant hypertension at higher doses. Low-dose oral minoxidil (typically 0.25mg to 5mg daily) is used off-label for hair loss with increasing frequency in dermatology practice. Several recent peer-reviewed studies support efficacy. Side-effect profile includes hypertrichosis (unwanted body hair), ankle swelling, and cardiovascular considerations at higher doses. Folik tracks oral minoxidil if prescribed; the Coach surfaces the off-label status, dose ranges from published studies, and known side-effect monitoring.

Can I use Folik for female pattern hair loss?

Yes. Folik supports the Ludwig scale for women (stages I, II, III) alongside the Norwood scale for men. The AI Coach surfaces female pattern hair loss evidence — minoxidil 2% and 5% topical (FDA-approved for women), spironolactone (off-label, commonly prescribed by dermatologists), low-level laser therapy, and microneedling. IMPORTANT: finasteride and dutasteride are FDA Pregnancy Category X and are NOT appropriate for women of childbearing potential due to fetal risk. The Coach surfaces this explicitly. For diffuse thinning in women, dermatologist evaluation is especially valuable because contributors like postpartum telogen effluvium, PCOS, thyroid dysfunction, iron deficiency, and restrictive dieting are common and warrant medical attention.

What if my hair loss is patchy or has skin changes?

Folik is built for pattern hair loss tracking (androgenetic alopecia) and progress monitoring on treatments. Patchy hair loss with smooth bald patches may indicate alopecia areata (autoimmune). Hair loss with skin redness, scarring, itching, burning, or scaling may indicate scarring alopecia (lichen planopilaris, frontal fibrosing alopecia, central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia). Sudden severe shedding may indicate telogen effluvium triggered by illness, medication, thyroid issue, or iron deficiency. None of these are diagnosable by an app. See a dermatologist for evaluation — early intervention matters more for these conditions than for pattern hair loss.

Does Folik track microneedling sessions?

Yes. Track at-home dermaroller sessions or in-office procedures. The Coach surfaces the published evidence on microneedling-minoxidil synergy (Dhurat et al. 2013 showed enhanced results vs minoxidil alone) and frequency guidance from published studies. Note: microneedling has technique requirements — needle length, frequency, skin preparation, post-care — and inappropriate technique can cause skin damage or infection. For first-time microneedling, dermatologist guidance is recommended.

Is Folik HIPAA compliant?

HIPAA applies to covered entities (providers, insurers, business associates) — not directly to consumer wellness apps you use yourself. Practically, Folik keeps your photos and tracking data on your device, requires no account for the free Norwood calculator, and routes AI Coach queries through a privacy proxy that does not link prompts to your identity. If you choose to share progress photos with your dermatologist, those become part of your medical record under their HIPAA obligations.

Does Folik upload my scalp photos to a server?

No. The photo journal is local-only — photos stay on your device. AI Coach queries are routed through a privacy proxy without identity linkage. We do not store scalp photos on Folik's servers and do not sell or share user data.

Can Folik help me decide on a hair transplant?

Folik tracks pre-transplant baseline (so you have evidence of what was there before), tracks the post-transplant timeline (initial shock loss, then growth phases at months 4–12 per ISHRS resources), and surfaces ISHRS guidance on evaluating clinics, expected outcomes, and complications. We do not refer to specific clinics — Folik has no commercial relationship with any transplant provider. For clinic selection, dermatology consult and ISHRS member directories are more useful than app recommendations.

What is the difference between the free Norwood calculator and the Premium AI Coach?

Free Norwood calculator: take or upload a photo, get a Norwood (men) or Ludwig (women) stage estimate. No signup, no paywall. Premium AI Coach: ask follow-up questions like "is this consistent with my family history of pattern loss", "what treatments does the AAD guideline recommend at this stage", "how does my pattern compare against the 18-month finasteride trial baseline cohort" — every answer cited. Premium also unlocks the full 5-angle calibrated photo journal with ghost overlay, treatment tracker, and progress trend charts.

How accurate is the AI Norwood/Ludwig staging?

The AI gives a reasonable estimate based on visible hairline position, crown coverage, and frontal density. It is a starting reference, not a diagnostic. Dermatologists trained in trichoscopy and clinical examination produce more accurate staging because they evaluate hair miniaturization patterns, density per cm², and pull-test results that no photo can capture. Use the AI staging as a starting reference and tracking baseline; rely on dermatology evaluation for clinical decisions.

How much does Folik cost?

Free Norwood/Ludwig calculator is permanently free with no signup. Premium subscription (price shown in the App Store at install, subject to App Store regional pricing) unlocks the AI Hair Loss Coach with cited sources, the full 5-angle calibrated photo journal with ghost overlay alignment, the treatment tracker, and progress trend charts. Subscriptions auto-renew unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the period ends. Manage in iPhone Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions.

What if I have a side effect from a treatment I am tracking in Folik?

Log the side effect in the treatment tracker. For non-urgent side effects, bring the log to your next dermatology appointment — having a structured timeline makes the conversation more productive. For sexual side effects on finasteride or dutasteride, contact your prescriber. For severe symptoms — severe scalp pain, signs of infection from microneedling, severe edema, chest pain, signs of allergic reaction — seek medical attention immediately: 911 in the US for emergencies, urgent care or your dermatologist's office for non-emergency concerns. Folik is a tracker, not a medical safety system.

Editorial · 2026 Ranking

# Best Hair Loss Tracker Apps 2026

Seven iPhone apps for adults tracking pattern hair loss — ranked honestly, including our own with full disclosure.

 See the ranking

Overview

## How we ranked these apps

If you've searched the App Store for "hair loss tracker" recently, you saw dozens of results that all look similar — most promising to "regrow your hair" with vague AI scoring. This is the ranking of seven apps that are actually worth installing in 2026, what each one does well, and which one fits which use case. We make one of these apps (Folik). We rank it where it deserves to be ranked.

Across seven apps we evaluated the features that matter to an actual person tracking pattern hair loss, not the features that look good on a marketing landing page:

- Norwood/Ludwig AI staging. Can the app give you a stage from a photo? Is the calculator free or behind a paywall?

- Photo journal quality. Does it support multiple angles? Calibrated framing (ghost overlay)? Pixel-density measurement? Side-by-side comparison?

- Treatment tracking. Reminders and logs for minoxidil (topical and oral), finasteride, dutasteride, microneedling, supplements, ketoconazole, LLLT.

- AI Coach. Can the app answer specific questions about treatments and side effects, and does it cite the sources?

- Source citation density. Generic marketing-level guidance vs specific AAD guideline section or PubMed study with year and authors.

- Honest off-label disclosure. Does the app surface that dutasteride is off-label for hair loss in the US? That oral minoxidil is off-label? That finasteride and dutasteride are FDA Pregnancy Category X?

- Privacy posture. Local-only photos vs cloud upload. Account required or anonymous.

- Female pattern hair loss support. Ludwig scale, women-specific treatment context, contraception/pregnancy warnings on finasteride.

- Pricing model. Free tier, subscription, what's behind the paywall.

None of these apps prescribe medication, diagnose hair loss type, or replace a dermatologist. We say this once and assume it for the rest.

### What none of these apps do

Important boundary. None of these apps — including ours — prescribe medication, diagnose hair loss type, or replace a dermatologist. They are companion tracking tools. The decisions about starting, continuing, titrating, or stopping finasteride, dutasteride, topical minoxidil, oral minoxidil, microneedling, or any treatment belong to you and your dermatologist.

Pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) is not the only kind of hair loss. Patchy bald spots with smooth skin may indicate alopecia areata. Hair loss with skin changes (redness, scarring, itching, scaling) may indicate scarring alopecia. Sudden severe shedding may indicate telogen effluvium from an underlying medical issue. These conditions warrant dermatology evaluation, not app tracking.

Finasteride and dutasteride are FDA Pregnancy Category X — pregnant women must not handle crushed or broken tablets. These medications cause serious birth defects. Women of childbearing potential should not use these medications.

For severe scalp pain, signs of infection from microneedling, severe allergic reaction, or sexual side effects on finasteride/dutasteride, contact your prescriber or call 911 for emergencies. For mental health crisis from body image concerns, call or text 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline).

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Why did you rank your own app first?

Folik ranks #1 because of two features no other app in this list matches simultaneously: a permanently free Norwood/Ludwig calculator with no signup, and an AI Coach that cites a specific source (AAD guideline, FDA document, named PubMed study) on every single reply. Regrow Hair AI has the larger user base and longer track record, which is why it sits at #2. Many users run both on the same phone — that is the honest recommendation. Full disclosure that Folik is our product is in the intro and in every section about it.

Is the free Norwood calculator in Folik really free?

Yes. The Norwood/Ludwig staging scan in Folik is permanently free with no account required. You take a photo, get a stage, and do not need to create a subscription or enter an email. The AI Coach and advanced photo journaling features are behind a subscription, but the Norwood/Ludwig calculator is not.

Does any app on this list replace a dermatologist?

No. None of these apps prescribe medication, provide a clinical diagnosis, or replace a board-certified dermatologist. They are tracking and educational tools. For diagnosis of hair loss type, for prescription-only medications (finasteride, dutasteride, oral minoxidil), or for conditions beyond androgenetic alopecia, see a dermatologist. Pattern hair loss apps are most useful after you have a diagnosis and a treatment plan — they help you track whether the plan is working.

What is the FDA Pregnancy Category X warning for finasteride and dutasteride?

Finasteride (Propecia®, Proscar®) and dutasteride (Avodart®) are classified as FDA Pregnancy Category X, meaning studies in animals or humans have shown fetal abnormalities and the risks outweigh any possible benefit. Pregnant women must not handle crushed or broken tablets, as the active ingredient can be absorbed through the skin. Women of childbearing potential should not use these medications. Folik explicitly surfaces this warning in the app; other apps in this list vary in how prominently they display it.

Is dutasteride approved by the FDA for hair loss?

No. Dutasteride (Avodart®) is FDA-approved for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), not for androgenetic alopecia in the United States. Its use for hair loss is off-label. It is approved for hair loss in some other countries (South Korea, Japan). Folik explicitly surfaces this off-label status when discussing dutasteride; not all apps in this ranking do. Always discuss off-label use with your prescribing physician.

Is oral minoxidil off-label for hair loss?

Yes. Oral minoxidil is FDA-approved for hypertension, not for hair loss. Topical minoxidil (Rogaine®) is FDA-approved for hair loss. Oral minoxidil is used off-label for androgenetic alopecia at low doses (0.25–5 mg/day for men, 0.25–1.25 mg/day for women) and is increasingly prescribed by dermatologists because it avoids the scalp irritation of topical application. As with all off-label medications, discuss with your prescribing physician. Folik surfaces this off-label disclosure explicitly.

Which apps store photos locally vs in the cloud?

Folik and Hair Plan both use local-only photo storage — scalp photos never leave your device unless you explicitly share them. HairMaxxing routes scan data through OpenAI's cloud API per their own App Store disclosure. Hair Loss AI Snap & Scanner may use tracking data across other companies' apps and websites per its App Store privacy label. Regrow Hair AI and Rooty — check their current App Store privacy labels for the most up-to-date data usage policies.

iOS App · Skin Health · Eczema

# Salvora — a calmer way to understand your eczema

Eczema flares rarely have one cause. It's the new detergent, the bad week of sleep, the cold snap and the skipped moisturizer — all at once. Salvora keeps flares, itch, sleep, triggers and care routines in one private record, tracks a POEM-style severity trend over time and builds a photo timeline that stays on your iPhone — so your next dermatology visit starts with a clear history.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone · iOS 17.0+ · no account · photos stay on your iPhone · 7-day free trial

Overview

## What is Salvora?

Salvora is an AI eczema tracker for people living with atopic dermatitis, recurring flares, dry or itchy skin and changing care routines — and for parents organizing a child's eczema history.

Eczema is a pattern condition. The single most useful thing you can bring to a dermatologist is a history: when flares happened, how bad they were, what changed beforehand and what you used on your skin. Memory is terrible at this — especially at 2 a.m. with an itching child.

Salvora records that history in a few taps: flare dates; itch, rash, dryness and sleep loss; food, allergy, stress, weather, product and routine triggers; creams, moisturizers, topical steroids and baths. A POEM-style self-reported severity score turns "it's been bad lately" into a trend line. Photos build a skin timeline that stays on your phone.

AI context, not a diagnosis. Opt-in AI can summarize patterns across your logs and photos so they are easier to review. Salvora does not diagnose eczema, identify diseases, prescribe treatment or replace a clinician. It can show you the warning signs published by the American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) and the National Eczema Association (NEA) and tell you when they warrant a call.

Audience

## Who Salvora is built for

### Adults with atopic dermatitis

Recurring flares, dry itchy skin, a shelf of creams you've half-tried. Build a history that shows what actually happens before a flare and what helps.

### Parents of a child with eczema

Organize your child's flares, sleep disruption, foods and care routines in one place — ready for the pediatrician or pediatric dermatologist.

### People who lose sleep to itch

Sleep loss is one of the most disruptive parts of eczema and one clinicians ask about. Track it next to flares and routines.

### Anyone testing a new routine

New moisturizer, new wash, a different bath routine? Record the change and see the POEM-style trend before and after.

### Before a dermatology or allergy visit

Export a summary with flare timeline, severity trend, symptom notes, triggers, care routines and photos.

### Privacy-first users

No account. Photos stored on your iPhone. AI analysis is opt-in. No ads and no third-party analytics.

Capabilities

## What Salvora tracks — and why each piece matters

- Flares and flare dates. The backbone of any eczema history. Log when a flare starts and how it progresses.

- Itch, rash, dry skin and sleep loss. The symptoms that shape daily life — including the nights lost to scratching.

- Trigger log. Food, allergy, stress, weather, products and routines. Over time Salvora helps you compare your flare history with the context you recorded.

- Care routine history. Creams, moisturizers, topical steroids, baths and other care steps — what you used, when, and how skin responded.

- POEM-style severity trend. A self-reported severity score modeled on the style of POEM (Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure), tracked over weeks so change is visible.

- Photo timeline on your iPhone. Dated photos and notes of your skin, stored on device. Slow change becomes visible; appointments become concrete.

- Opt-in AI pattern summaries. When you choose, AI summarizes patterns across logs and photos so records are easier to review. Context, not diagnosis.

- Doctor-ready summary + warning signs. Flare timeline, severity trend, symptom notes, trigger log, care history and photo timeline in one summary. AAD- and NEA-published warning signs show when to call a clinician.

Workflow

## How to build an eczema history your dermatologist can use — a 6-week framework

Eczema changes over weeks. This is the rhythm Salvora is built around.

- Day 1 — baseline.Record today's skin: where it's affected, itch, sleep last night, and a POEM-style severity score. Take baseline photos of the affected areas. List your current care routine.

- Daily — a 30-second log.Itch, sleep, anything unusual (new product, stress, weather change, new food), and what you applied. Short and consistent beats detailed and occasional.

- When a flare starts — log it immediately.Mark the flare, add a photo, note what changed in the previous 48 hours. This is where trigger patterns come from.

- Weekly — severity score and review.Log a weekly POEM-style score and look at the trend. If AI summaries are on, review what patterns it highlights — as questions, not conclusions.

- Before the appointment — export.Export the doctor-ready summary. Bring questions about what the trend shows, which triggers seem to recur and how your routine could change.

In the wild

## Real scenarios where Salvora earns its keep

### The winter flare mystery

Rachel's hands flared every December. Six weeks of logging in Salvora showed the flares started days after switching to a heavier-scented hand soap at work and worsened with cold, dry weather — a combination she could finally bring to her dermatologist.

### A toddler's bad nights

Ben and Ola logged their two-year-old's itch, sleep, foods and moisturizer routine. The summary they exported showed sleep loss tracked closely with flares on the legs — and gave the pediatric dermatologist a clear timeline instead of exhausted guesses.

### Leaving EczemaWise

Sam had used EczemaWise for years and saw the sunset notice. She started a fresh record in Salvora with baseline photos and her current routine so her history continues without a gap.

### Testing a new routine

After her dermatologist suggested a new moisturizer routine, Lina tracked her POEM-style score weekly. Four weeks later the trend — and the photo timeline — made the follow-up conversation simple.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

What is Salvora?

Salvora is an educational AI eczema tracker for iPhone. It records flares, itch, rash, sleep, foods, triggers and care routines, tracks a POEM-style severity trend, keeps a photo timeline on your iPhone and exports a doctor-ready summary.

Can Salvora diagnose eczema?

No. Salvora does not diagnose eczema, identify diseases, prescribe treatment or replace a clinician. Its optional AI summarizes patterns in your own logs and photos so they're easier to review.

What is POEM?

POEM (Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure) is a widely used questionnaire in which patients rate eczema symptoms such as itch, sleep disturbance, bleeding, weeping, cracking, flaking and dryness over the past week. Salvora uses a POEM-style self-reported severity score to show your trend over time; it is for personal tracking, not a clinical assessment.

Can Salvora find my eczema triggers?

It helps you compare your flare history with the context you recorded — foods, stress, weather, allergens, products and routines. Triggers become clearer over weeks of consistent logging. Suspected food allergies should be evaluated by an allergist rather than by elimination alone.

Can I use Salvora for my child?

Yes. Parents can organize a child's eczema history — flares, sleep disruption, foods, care routines and photos — and share the summary with a pediatrician, pediatric dermatologist or allergist.

Where are my photos stored?

Photos are stored on your iPhone. No account is required, AI analysis is opt-in, and there are no ads or third-party analytics.

EczemaWise is shutting down — can Salvora replace it?

EczemaWise has ended new account creation and existing users can continue only through December 18, 2026. Salvora covers the core jobs — flares, triggers, care routines, a severity trend and a doctor-ready summary — in a private, on-device record. Start with baseline photos and your current routine so your history continues.

How much does Salvora cost?

Salvora Pro is $39.99 per year or $7.99 per week in the US, each with a 7-day free trial for eligible Apple IDs. Both plans unlock the same features and auto-renew unless cancelled at least 24 hours before renewal.

When should I contact a clinician urgently?

Contact a clinician promptly for signs of skin infection — spreading redness, warmth, pus, yellow crusting, or painful clustered blisters (which can signal eczema herpeticum and needs same-day care) — or for fever, rapidly worsening skin, or a flare that doesn't respond to your usual plan. Call 911 or your local emergency number for allergic reactions with swelling of the face or throat or difficulty breathing.

Across 6 apps we evaluated the features that matter to an actual user, not the ones that look good on a landing page:

- Flare tracking. Dates, severity and progression.

- Trigger logging. Food, stress, weather, allergens, products and routines — and how the app helps you compare them with flares.

- Severity measurement. A structured score (such as a POEM-style measure) rather than vague impressions.

- Photo timeline. Dated photos, and where they are stored.

- Doctor usefulness. A summary a dermatologist or pediatrician can read quickly.

- Privacy and longevity. Account requirements, analytics, and whether the app will still be around.

None of these apps diagnose eczema or replace a dermatologist, allergist or pediatrician. We say this once and assume it for the rest.

iOS App · Women's Health · PCOS

# Cysta AI — one clear place for everything PCOS

Irregular periods, symptoms, meals, weight, supplements, fertility questions and lab results usually live in five different apps and a notes file. Cysta AI puts them in one PCOS-specific tracker, lets you ask an evidence-informed AI Coach about your own patterns, and turns the records you choose into a doctor-ready PDF.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone · iOS 17.0+ · 7-day free trial on Weekly · 20 languages

Overview

## What is Cysta AI?

Cysta AI is a PCOS tracking app for people with polycystic ovary syndrome who want symptoms, cycles, food, weight, fertility context and bloodwork in one place — and a clearer summary to bring to their doctor.

PCOS is not one symptom. It is irregular or absent periods, acne, unwanted hair growth or hair thinning, weight changes, insulin resistance, and — for many people — questions about fertility. Generic period trackers are built around a predictable 28-day cycle; PCOS cycles often are not predictable. Cysta AI is built around PCOS specifically, so irregular cycles are the expected case, not an error.

It is organizational, not clinical. Cysta AI does not diagnose PCOS, does not prescribe metformin, inositol, spironolactone or any treatment, and does not replace a gynecologist or endocrinologist. It helps you keep an honest record and prepare better questions — the decisions stay with you and your clinician.

What makes it different: most PCOS apps are either a meal-plan program or a cycle predictor. Cysta AI is a tracker first — cycles, symptoms, meals, weight, supplements, a photo journal for visible changes, TTC signs and lab panels in one timeline — with an AI Coach that reads your recorded context and can show the sources behind its educational answers.

Audience

## Who Cysta AI is built for

### Newly diagnosed with PCOS

You left the appointment with a diagnosis and a handful of pamphlets. Start logging cycles, symptoms and meals from day one so the follow-up visit has three months of real data instead of guesses.

### Irregular or absent periods

Standard period apps keep "predicting" a period that does not come. Cysta AI records what actually happened — flow, spotting, gaps — so the pattern your doctor sees is the true one.

### Trying to conceive with PCOS

Log ovulation signs and TTC context alongside cycle history, see your estimated fertile window, and bring an organized record to a fertility consultation.

### Managing insulin resistance through food

Meals, food notes, weight and supplements in the same timeline as symptoms. Ask the Coach about diet and insulin resistance, and see how your routines line up with how you feel.

### Tracking acne and hair changes

The photo journal follows visible changes — acne, hirsutism, hair thinning — over months, which is how slow hormonal changes actually become visible.

### Keeping lab results in one place

Scan bloodwork or enter it manually — testosterone, SHBG, AMH, HbA1c, lipids, whatever your doctor ordered — and keep every panel organized next to the symptoms it relates to.

Capabilities

## What Cysta AI does for people with PCOS

- Cycle tracking built for irregular cycles. Record flow, spotting and gaps without the app assuming a textbook 28-day rhythm. Review cycle history over months to see the real pattern — the thing your gynecologist actually asks about.

- Symptom, meal, weight and supplement log. Log PCOS symptoms, meals and food notes, weight and supplement routines in one daily flow. Everything lands on the same timeline, so you can compare what changed before a good or a bad week.

- Photo journal for visible changes. Acne, unwanted hair growth and hair thinning change slowly. A dated photo journal makes slow change visible and gives you something concrete to show at an appointment.

- TTC context and estimated fertile window. Track ovulation signs and trying-to-conceive context alongside your cycle history. The fertile window is an estimate from your own records — useful for planning, not a contraceptive method.

- Lab results — scanned or typed. Scan a bloodwork report or enter results manually, then keep each panel organized. Values stay next to the symptoms and routines they relate to, instead of in a PDF you cannot find.

- Evidence-informed AI Coach. Ask about PCOS symptoms, diet, insulin resistance, hormones, cycle changes, fertility and everyday routines. The Coach uses the context you recorded, organizes educational guidance and can show supporting sources. It helps you understand patterns and prepare questions — it does not make medical decisions.

- Doctor-ready PDF summary. Choose which records to include and export a clean summary for your gynecologist, endocrinologist, dietitian or fertility clinic.

- Consent-first AI. Cysta AI asks for clear consent before AI features process Coach messages, photos or lab images. Reminders help you stay consistent with the records that matter to your routine.

Workflow

## How to track PCOS in a way your doctor can actually use — a 90-day framework

PCOS management is measured in months, not days. This is the workflow Cysta AI is built around.

- Day 1 — set your baseline.Log where you are today: last period date, current symptoms, weight, supplements and any medication your doctor has already prescribed. If you have recent bloodwork, scan it in. A baseline is what makes month three meaningful.

- Weeks 1–4 — log lightly, every day.A short daily check-in beats a detailed weekly one. Symptoms, meals, flow or spotting, and anything unusual — sleep, stress, a new supplement. Use reminders so the habit survives a busy week.

- Weeks 4–8 — start asking questions.Once there are a few weeks of data, ask the AI Coach about what you see: "Do my symptoms cluster around certain meals?" "What does research say about inositol and cycle regularity?" Treat answers as education and material for your next appointment.

- Month 2–3 — review trends, add photos and labs.Look at cycle history, symptoms, meals, weight and photo-journal entries together. If your clinician ordered follow-up labs, add them next to the first panel.

- Before the appointment — export the PDF.Pick the records that matter and export a doctor-ready summary. Bring your questions. A clinician can do far more with 90 days of organized records than with "my periods are kind of irregular".

## Frequently asked questions

What is Cysta AI?

Cysta AI is a PCOS tracking app for iPhone. It keeps PCOS symptoms, irregular cycles, meals, weight, supplements, a photo journal, TTC context and lab results in one place, adds an evidence-informed AI Coach that uses your recorded context, and exports a doctor-ready PDF. It is for informational, educational and organizational purposes only.

Can Cysta AI diagnose PCOS?

No. Cysta AI is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat PCOS. PCOS is diagnosed by a clinician, typically using criteria that combine cycle history, signs or blood tests for elevated androgens, and ultrasound findings, after ruling out other causes. Cysta AI helps you organize the information that conversation needs.

Does it work if my periods are very irregular or absent?

Yes — that is the main reason it exists. Cysta AI records what actually happens (flow, spotting, gaps) rather than assuming a regular cycle, so long or absent cycles show up accurately in your history. Absent periods for three months or more are worth raising with a clinician.

What does the AI Coach do?

You can ask about PCOS symptoms, diet, insulin resistance, hormones, cycle changes, fertility and everyday routines. The Coach uses the context you recorded, organizes educational guidance and can show supporting sources. It is designed to help you understand patterns and prepare questions, not to make medical decisions for you.

Can I track lab results for PCOS?

Yes. Scan a bloodwork report or enter values manually, and Cysta AI keeps each panel organized next to your symptom and cycle history. Interpretation of lab values for your situation belongs to your clinician; the app keeps them in one place and helps you prepare questions.

Is Cysta AI useful when trying to conceive?

Yes. Track TTC context and ovulation signs alongside your cycle history and see an estimated fertile window. With irregular PCOS cycles, any fertile window estimate is less certain — it is a planning aid, not a guarantee and not a contraceptive method. A fertility specialist can advise on ovulation testing and treatment.

How is Cysta AI different from Flo or Clue?

Flo and Clue are excellent general cycle trackers with very large user bases. Cysta AI is narrower: it is built around PCOS, keeps lab results and a photo journal for visible changes in the same record, and includes an AI Coach that reads your own logs. Many people with PCOS use a general tracker for years before switching to something PCOS-specific.

How is Cysta AI different from PCOS Pal or Cysterhood?

PCOS Pal and Cysterhood are structured programs — lessons, meal plans, recipes, workouts and coaching. Cysta AI is a tracker and organizer: it does not give you a meal plan, but it records what you eat, how you feel, your cycles and your labs in one timeline for you and your clinician. Some people use a program and a tracker together.

What happens to my photos and lab images?

Cysta AI requests clear consent before AI features process Coach messages, photos or lab images. See the privacy policy linked in the App Store listing for full detail on storage and processing.

How much does Cysta AI cost?

When should I see a doctor instead of using an app?

See a clinician for a PCOS diagnosis or treatment decisions, periods absent for three months or more, very heavy bleeding, severe pelvic pain, signs of pregnancy complications, or rapid unexplained weight change. For severe pain, heavy bleeding with dizziness or fainting, call 911 or your local emergency number.

### What none of these apps do

None of these apps — including ours — diagnose PCOS, prescribe metformin, inositol, spironolactone, hormonal contraception or fertility treatment, or replace a gynecologist, endocrinologist or reproductive specialist. They are tracking, education and program tools.

iOS App · Liver Health · Fatty Liver (MASLD)

# Hepatica — your doctor said "fatty liver". Here's what to do next.

Fatty liver is often found by accident — a slightly high ALT on a routine blood test, a comment on an ultrasound — followed by "lose some weight and eat better". Hepatica turns that into something you can act on: it explains your liver blood tests against your own report, calculates FIB-4 when the values are there, shows how each meal fits a liver-friendly diet, and prepares the questions for your next appointment.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone · iOS 17.0+ · no account · records stay on device · 7-day free trial on Weekly

Overview

## What is Hepatica?

Hepatica is an educational wellness app for people with fatty liver — now often called MASLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease), formerly NAFLD — who want to understand their blood tests, eat in a liver-friendly way and arrive at appointments prepared.

Fatty liver is one of the most common liver conditions in the world, and for most people it is silent. There is usually no pain and no obvious symptom — just numbers on a lab report most people have never been taught to read. Hepatica starts there: photograph the report, import the PDF or type the values, and each one is explained in plain language against the reference range printed on your own report — not a generic range from the internet.

When the needed values are present (age, AST, ALT and platelets), Hepatica calculates FIB-4, a screening index many clinicians use to decide whether further testing for liver scarring is needed. It is shown for education and discussion with your clinician — not as a diagnosis.

Then there is food. Hepatica looks at a photo of your plate, names what it sees and explains what makes the meal a better or harder fit for a liver-friendly diet — added sugar, frying, refined carbohydrates, fiber — with one practical swap. If the photo isn't a meal, it says so instead of scoring it.

What it is not: Hepatica is not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat or cure any disease and does not replace your doctor or hepatologist. AI can be incomplete or wrong.

Audience

## Who Hepatica is built for

### Newly told "you have fatty liver"

Start with the lab report you already have. Understand each value, see your FIB-4 if it can be calculated, and set one goal for the next test.

### Watching ALT and AST between tests

Add each new test and see every value next to the last one. Progress is easier to believe when it's on the same screen.

### On a GLP-1 medicine

Weight loss is one of the main levers for fatty liver. Track weight, meals and labs together while on Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro or Zepbound as prescribed.

### Watching blood sugar or living with PCOS

Insulin resistance and fatty liver often travel together. Keep HbA1c and liver values in one history.

### Rebuilding after alcohol

Alcohol-free days are tracked without judgment and can be hidden from Progress at any time. Stopping heavy drinking can require medical support — talk to a doctor first.

### Preparing for a hepatology visit

Export a doctor summary with your results, your saved questions and the habits behind them.

Capabilities

## What Hepatica does for people with fatty liver

- Blood tests, explained against your own report. ALT, AST, GGT, ALP, bilirubin, platelets, HbA1c and more — each explained in plain language using the reference range printed on your report. Photo, PDF import or manual entry.

- FIB-4 calculated when possible. When age, AST, ALT and platelets are available, Hepatica calculates FIB-4 — a screening index your doctor may use to decide on further tests such as elastography. Shown for education and discussion, never as a verdict.

- Test-over-test comparison. Add your next test and see each value next to the previous one. Fatty liver improves over months; seeing the trend keeps you going.

- Meal photo check with one practical swap. Photograph your plate. Hepatica names what it sees, explains what makes it a better or harder fit for a liver-friendly diet and suggests one realistic swap. Not-a-meal photos are not scored.

- AI Liver Guide with sources. Ask about results, food, alcohol or medicines. Answers draw on published clinical guidelines and public health sources, show where they come from, and use your saved goal and records. It explains and helps you prepare questions; it does not diagnose.

- One honest record. Evening check-ins, weekly goals, meals, alcohol-free days, medicines, weight and symptoms in one filterable history.

- Doctor summary PDF. Results, saved questions and the habits behind them — share before or during a visit.

- Private by default. No account. Records kept on your device. AI analysis of photos and text you choose happens only after consent; not used for advertising. No ads, no data selling.

Workflow

## How to work on fatty liver between blood tests — a 3-month framework

Liver blood tests are often repeated every few months. This is the loop Hepatica is built around, so each test tells you something.

- Day 1 — understand your starting point.Add your most recent lab report. Read what each value means against your own reference ranges. If FIB-4 can be calculated, note it and write down the question: "Do I need further testing for scarring?"

- Week 1 — pick one goal.Hepatica starts from your goal — newly diagnosed, weight, blood sugar, GLP-1, PCOS or alcohol. Choose one weekly goal you can actually keep, such as fewer sugary drinks or more alcohol-free days.

- Weeks 1–12 — check meals, check in each evening.Photograph meals when you're unsure and try the suggested swap. A short evening check-in records meals, alcohol-free days, medicines, weight and symptoms. Consistency beats perfection.

- Along the way — ask the Liver Guide."Is coffee OK for fatty liver?" "What does my GGT mean?" "Can I drink at all?" Save the answers and questions that matter for your appointment.

- Next blood test — compare and export.Add the new results and compare each value with the last. Export the doctor summary with results, questions and habits, and discuss next steps with your clinician.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

What is Hepatica?

Hepatica is an educational wellness app for people with fatty liver (MASLD, formerly NAFLD). It explains liver blood tests against your own report's reference ranges, calculates FIB-4 when possible, checks how meals fit a liver-friendly diet, answers questions through an AI Liver Guide with sources, and creates a doctor summary PDF.

What is the difference between NAFLD and MASLD?

They describe essentially the same condition. In 2023 international liver societies renamed non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), to emphasize its link with metabolic factors such as excess weight, insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Many doctors and reports still use both names.

Which blood tests does Hepatica understand?

ALT, AST, GGT, ALP, bilirubin, platelets, HbA1c and more. Each value is explained in plain language against the reference range printed on your own report. Import by photo, PDF or manual entry.

What is FIB-4 and does Hepatica calculate it?

FIB-4 is a screening index calculated from age, AST, ALT and platelet count. Clinicians use it to estimate whether significant liver scarring (fibrosis) is unlikely or whether further testing, such as elastography, is warranted. Hepatica calculates it when all needed values are present, for education and discussion with your clinician — it is not a diagnosis.

Can I reverse fatty liver with diet?

For many people, clinical guidelines point to gradual weight loss, better diet quality, physical activity and limiting alcohol as the core of managing fatty liver. How much and how fast depends on your situation — discuss targets with your clinician. Hepatica helps you track the habits and see whether your blood tests move.

Does Hepatica tell me what to eat?

It checks a meal you photograph and explains what makes it a better or harder fit for a liver-friendly diet — added sugar, frying, refined carbohydrates, fiber — with one practical swap. It does not prescribe a meal plan.

Is alcohol tracking judgmental?

No. Alcohol-free days are tracked in a neutral way and can be hidden from Progress at any time. Important: stopping heavy drinking suddenly can be dangerous and may require medical support — talk to a doctor first.

Where is my data stored?

No account is required and your records are kept on your device. After your consent, the photos and text you choose to analyse are processed by a cloud AI service and are not used for advertising. No ads and no data selling.

How much does Hepatica cost?

In the US, Hepatica Plus is $7.99 per week with a 7-day free trial for eligible new subscribers, or $39.99 per year (billed at purchase, no trial). Local prices are shown before purchase.

When should I seek urgent care?

Seek emergency care for vomiting blood, yellowing of the skin or eyes, confusion or unusual drowsiness, severe abdominal pain, or a rapidly swelling abdomen. These are not symptoms to track in an app.

# Best Fatty Liver Apps 2026

Six iPhone apps for people with fatty liver (MASLD, formerly NAFLD) — ranked honestly, including our own with full disclosure.

Overview

## How we ranked these apps

Fatty liver apps barely existed two years ago; now there are a dozen, almost all with small review counts. Most focus on food scoring. Very few help with the other half of the problem — understanding the blood tests that started it all. This ranking covers six apps worth trying and who each is for.

Across 6 apps we evaluated the features that matter to an actual user, not the ones that look good on a landing page:

- Lab understanding. Can the app read your report and explain ALT, AST, GGT and platelets against your own reference ranges? Does it calculate FIB-4?

- Meal guidance. Photo scoring, nutrient budgets, barcode scanning — and whether the advice is practical.

- Guidance quality. Is there an AI or expert guide, and does it show sources?

- Doctor usefulness. Can you export a summary for your GP or hepatologist?

- Stage coverage. Early fatty liver vs advanced disease (cirrhosis, ascites) needs different tracking.

- Privacy. Account requirements and where your records live.

None of these apps diagnose liver disease or replace a doctor or hepatologist. We say this once and assume it for the rest.

iOS App · Digestive Health · GERD & LPR

# Refluxora — the reflux tracker that remembers your throat

Most reflux apps track heartburn and stop there. Silent reflux (LPR) shows up as throat clearing, hoarseness, a lump-in-the-throat feeling or chronic cough — often with no heartburn at all. Refluxora keeps meals, classic GERD symptoms and throat or voice symptom scores in one record, helps you think through a meal from a photo, and exports a clean report for your appointment.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone · iOS 17.0+ · no account required · 7-day free trial on Weekly · 20 languages

Overview

## What is Refluxora?

Refluxora is an educational tracking app for people with GERD or LPR (silent reflux) who want to understand meals, symptoms and lab results — and keep the useful details in one place for their doctor or ENT.

Reflux is personal. Coffee wrecks one person's evening and does nothing to another. Generic "foods to avoid" lists help at the start, but what actually matters is your own pattern — which is only visible if meals and symptoms are recorded together, over time.

Refluxora starts with one question at a time: describe a meal or take a photo of it, photograph a lab result you already have, or record how you feel. It gives an explanation where it can, saves the observation and shows a clear next step. It is honest about limits — one photo cannot reveal every ingredient or establish your personal triggers, and missing lab units or reference ranges are never guessed.

What it is not: Refluxora does not diagnose GERD, LPR, Barrett's esophagus or anything else, does not prescribe PPIs, H2 blockers or alginates, and does not replace a gastroenterologist or ENT. AI output may be incomplete or incorrect. It is a tracker and an explainer that makes the appointment more useful.

Audience

## Who Refluxora is built for

### People with classic heartburn (GERD)

Burning after meals, worse lying down, a sour taste. Log meals and symptoms together and see which evenings go badly — instead of guessing.

### People with silent reflux (LPR)

Throat clearing, hoarseness, postnasal drip feeling, chronic cough, a lump in the throat. Refluxora includes throat and voice symptom scores — the things an ENT will ask about.

### Singers, teachers and heavy voice users

When your voice is your job, hoarseness is not a minor symptom. Track voice scores alongside meals, late eating and other factors you record.

### Newly told to "watch your diet"

Explore a meal before or after you eat it and get one practical food consideration — fat content, acidity, portion or timing — rather than a 200-item forbidden list.

### Preparing for a GI or ENT appointment

Export a report of meals, symptoms and throat scores so the specialist sees weeks of data, not a two-minute recollection.

### Privacy-minded users

No app account required. Selected text and photos are processed in the cloud only after your consent.

Capabilities

## What Refluxora does that most reflux apps don't

- Throat and voice symptom scores for LPR. Silent reflux is under-served by heartburn-only apps. Record throat and voice symptoms as scores next to meals and classic GERD symptoms, so LPR patterns become visible.

- Make sense of a meal — from a photo or a sentence. Explore ingredients and get a practical food consideration. Mark whether you planned or ate the meal, then add how you felt afterwards. Over time, your own records say more than any generic list.

- Understand an existing lab result. Choose a photo of a result you already have, review the recognized values and confirm them with one tap. Get an educational explanation and questions to discuss with your clinician. Missing units and reference ranges are not guessed.

- Ask about your own records. Discuss a saved observation with the AI assistant. Medical explanations use relevant source material; when information is missing, the assistant can ask for more context. You choose which records to share.

- See everything you've recorded. Meals, symptoms and throat or voice scores live together. Clearly labelled example data shows how a history grows — it is never presented as a prediction about your health.

- Appointment report. Export your observations as a report for a gastroenterologist, ENT or primary care visit.

Workflow

## How to find your reflux triggers — a 4-week tracking framework

Food and symptom diaries are one of the most practical tools for reflux. This is the simple routine Refluxora is designed for.

- Week 1 — record, don't change anything.Log what you eat and how you feel, including throat and voice symptoms if you have them. Note timing — late dinners and lying down soon after eating matter as much as the food itself. Resist the urge to cut everything at once.

- Week 2 — explore the meals that worry you.Photograph or describe the meals you suspect. Read the food consideration, eat as planned, then record how you felt 1–3 hours later. Mark meals as planned or eaten so you can see intention versus reality.

- Week 3 — test one change at a time.Pick one variable — an earlier dinner, smaller portions, less coffee — and keep everything else stable for a few days. One change at a time is the only way to learn what actually helps you.

- Week 4 — review and ask.Look back at your meals, symptoms and throat scores. Ask the AI assistant about specific saved observations. Write down the questions it helps you form.

- Before your appointment — export the report.Bring the report to your gastroenterologist or ENT. If you are already on a PPI or other medication, note how symptoms changed since starting it — that is exactly what the specialist needs.

Comparison

### The singer with a morning croak

Dana, a choir teacher, woke up hoarse most mornings but rarely had heartburn. After three weeks of logging meals and voice scores in Refluxora, the pattern pointed at late, heavy dinners. She brought the report to her ENT, who had already suspected LPR — now with data to back it.
