 | Best for | Homeowners, renters, parents, pet owners | Naturalists, gardeners, hikers | Citizen scientists | General curiosity

Where Picture Insect wins: Picture Insect has a global insect encyclopedia with 400× more species than PestSnap. If you are walking in the woods and want to know the species, life cycle, habitat, and native/invasive status of a beautiful longhorn beetle — Picture Insect is built for that, and PestSnap is not trying to displace it. Picture Insect also has a more developed gallery and sharing experience, an established community, and a free tier with limited daily identifications.

Where PestSnap wins: When you find something on the kitchen counter at 11 p.m., "Periplaneta americana" is not what you need. "American cockroach — moderate infestation risk, here are three traps that work, here is how to find an exterminator" is what you need. PestSnap returns the second. It also has three modes Picture Insect does not have: Scan the Bite, Scan the Evidence, Scan on Pet. The decision in one sentence: if you want to learn about a bug, get Picture Insect. If you want to deal with a bug, get PestSnap.

In the wild

## Real scenarios where PestSnap earns its keep

### The 2 a.m. bedbug scare

Sarah wakes up with three small red welts on the back of her wrist, arranged almost in a line. Her partner has none; her city apartment is on the third floor. She opens PestSnap, selects Scan the Bite, photographs the cluster. The app returns: bite pattern (line of three, exposed skin during sleep, delayed welt onset) consistent with bed bug behavior. The next step is not to throw out the mattress — it is to scan for evidence. Sarah uses Scan the Evidence on the mattress seams. Rust-colored smears. She calls a licensed exterminator. One night of bites is not proof; a pattern of bites with confirmed evidence is.

### The tick on the dog after a hike

Alex gets back from a trail hike with his retriever. During a post-hike check he finds something attached behind the dog's ear. He opens Scan on Pet, photographs the parasite on the fur. The app returns: deer tick — attached, Lyme-endemic region flagged. It surfaces the Pet Poison Helpline (1-855-764-7661) and recommends a vet visit if the tick was attached for more than 24 hours. Alex removes it with tweezers, photographs the removed tick, confirms deer tick, calls the vet. The app links to Poison Control guidance for tick removal on pets.

### The mud tubes in the basement

A homeowner finds what looks like small dirt tubes along a basement wall, connecting the soil to a wooden beam. She opens Scan the Evidence, photographs the tubes. PestSnap returns: subterranean termite mud tubes — infestation risk. It does not suggest a $12 spray. It goes straight to the exterminator finder with a note that subterranean termite damage requires professional treatment and an in-person scope of the damage before any quote is meaningful. She books two estimates through the app. Both confirm active termites.

### The pantry mystery

A small white moth flutters out of a rice bag. Scan the Bug: Indian meal moth — pantry infestation. The DIY method list is specific: freeze affected dry goods for 72 hours, seal remaining goods in airtight containers, use pheromone traps near the moth trail. No call to an exterminator needed; PestSnap is honest about which infestations are DIY-manageable and which are not.

How to identify a bite on your skin

When the bug is gone but the bites remain, five questions narrow down the culprit before you book a doctor visit:

- Count the bites and check the pattern.Bed bug bites typically appear in a line or zigzag of three (the "breakfast, lunch, dinner" pattern); mosquito bites are scattered; flea bites cluster around ankles and lower legs; tick bites are usually a single isolated puncture, often with the tick still attached.

- Check the location on your body.Bed bugs favor exposed skin during sleep (face, neck, arms, hands); mosquitoes hit any exposed skin equally; fleas dominate ankles and below-knee areas; ticks hide in warm folds (groin, armpits, scalp behind ears).

- Compare welt size and appearance.Mosquito welts are immediate, raised, and fade within 24 hours. Bed bug welts appear 1–2 days after the bite, are firmer, with a darker center dot. Flea bites are small (2–5 mm), pink-red, with a slight halo. Tick bites are usually flat with a small reddish dot at the attachment site.

- Check the timing.Bed bug bites appear after sleeping in the same room, night after night. Mosquito bites peak at dusk outdoors. Flea bites accumulate after sitting on carpet or near a pet bed. Tick bites follow hikes, dog walks, or gardening in tall grass.

- Watch for red flags that override everything.Bullseye rash (possible Lyme disease), rapidly spreading redness, fluid-filled or blackening blister, fever, chills, headache, muscle cramping within hours to days of a bite, or any allergic-reaction symptoms (difficulty breathing, throat swelling, widespread hives) — stop the app and call 911 or Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Do not stop to take a photo.

PestSnap's Scan the Bite mode automates this five-question workflow. It covers about 80% of bite-identification cases. What no app should do — and what PestSnap explicitly does not do — is diagnose Lyme disease, cellulitis, or anaphylaxis. For those, the right path is always a doctor.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

What is PestSnap?

PestSnap is an iPhone app that uses AI vision to identify common US home pests, bites on human skin, droppings and other pest evidence, and parasites on dogs and cats. You point your camera at the bug, the bite, the evidence, or your pet, and within about three seconds the app returns a plain-English verdict and the next step you should take — a DIY method or a licensed exterminator. It is published by Loveiko Labs and costs $4.99 per week or $39.99 per year with a 7-day free trial.

What are the four scan modes in PestSnap?

Scan the Bug (photograph the insect or pest itself), Scan the Bite (photograph the bite pattern on human skin), Scan the Evidence (photograph droppings, mud tubes, holes in pantry, or other physical traces), and Scan on Pet (photograph a tick, flea, lice, or mite on a dog or cat). Three of the four modes — Bite, Evidence, On Pet — are not available in Picture Insect, iNaturalist, or Seek.

How many pests does PestSnap identify?

25+ of the most common US household pests across six categories: crawling pests (cockroach, bed bug, silverfish, earwig), biting and stinging insects (mosquito, tick, flea, wasp, bee, fire ant), spiders (house spider, wolf spider, brown recluse, black widow), structural pests (termite, carpenter ant, carpenter bee, powder post beetle), pantry pests (fruit fly, drain fly, pantry moth, weevil), and outdoor visitors (hornet, yellowjacket, stink bug, boxelder bug). We focus on what people find inside their homes, not the 10,000+ species global insect catalog.

How accurate is PestSnap?

PestSnap is built on a current-generation multimodal AI vision model and returns high-confidence identifications for the 25+ pests it covers when given a clear, well-lit photo from a reasonable distance. Accuracy drops with blurry photos, poor lighting, partial captures, unusual angles, and edge species like rare regional pests or larval stages. We do not claim 100% accuracy, and we do not think any photo-based bug ID app should. For confirmed infestations or before paying for treatment, always verify with a licensed exterminator's in-person inspection.

Can PestSnap identify what bit me from a photo of the bite?

Yes, with caveats. Scan the Bite analyzes the bite pattern (cluster size and arrangement), distribution on the body (linear, random, exposed-skin-only), and surrounding skin reaction (welt size, color, halo) and matches them against documented patterns for bed bugs, mosquitoes, fleas, ticks, and spiders. It returns the most likely culprit plus what to watch for. This is identification reference only, not medical advice. Any bite with severe swelling, fever, a bullseye rash, spreading redness, or any allergic-reaction symptom needs a doctor, not an app. Call 911 or Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) for any bite with concerning symptoms.

What is the difference between PestSnap and Picture Insect?

Picture Insect (by Glority) is the most-installed bug identifier on the App Store and is excellent at what it does — naming any of 10,000+ insect species and giving a naturalist-style encyclopedia entry. PestSnap is built for a different job. It covers a tighter list (25+ common US home pests) and returns a homeowner-style verdict — harmless, nuisance, or infestation risk — plus 3-5 specific DIY methods and a one-tap exterminator finder. PestSnap also has Scan the Bite, Scan the Evidence, and Scan on Pet modes that Picture Insect does not have. Pick Picture Insect if you want to learn entomology. Pick PestSnap if you want to deal with a roach in the kitchen at 11 p.m.

Does PestSnap work on bed bugs?

Yes — bed bugs are one of the most-scanned pests in the app, in all four modes. Scan the Bug works on the bed bug itself; Scan the Bite works on the characteristic three-in-a-line bite pattern on exposed skin overnight; Scan the Evidence works on the rust-colored fecal spots on mattress seams and box springs. If the verdict comes back as bed bug, the next step is almost always a professional treatment — bed bugs are notoriously hard to DIY out of a unit, and PestSnap will say so rather than pretend a $20 spray solves it.

Can PestSnap identify ticks on my dog?

Yes — that is what Scan on Pet is for. Photograph the parasite while it is on your pet, or once removed onto a paper towel. PestSnap identifies whether it is a tick (and which species — deer tick, dog tick, lone star tick when visible), a flea, a louse, a mite, or sometimes something less alarming like a tick-shaped scab. For ticks attached longer than 24 hours, especially deer ticks in Lyme-endemic regions, the app links to Pet Poison Helpline (1-855-764-7661) and recommends a vet visit. This is not a substitute for a vet visit.

What does Scan the Evidence identify?

Physical traces of pests — what is left behind when the pest itself is hiding. The most common scans are: cockroach droppings (small dark grain-like specks near food sources), mouse and rat droppings (larger, distinct shape), termite mud tubes on foundations or basements, bed bug fecal smears on mattress seams, carpenter ant frass (sawdust-like debris), and pantry moth webbing in dry-goods packaging. Knowing what is leaving the trace is often more useful than seeing the bug itself, because evidence tells you whether there is a population, not just a stray individual.

Is the photo I take stored anywhere?

PestSnap processes scan photos through a third-party AI vision provider for the identification itself; we do not retain the photo on our servers beyond the scan request, and we do not link photos to identifying information. Full details are in the privacy policy. If you are scanning bites on skin and want extra caution, you can use the camera in well-cropped mode to avoid capturing face or other identifying features.

How much does PestSnap cost?

$4.99 per week or $39.99 per year, both with a 7-day free trial. The weekly tier is for the renter who needs the app for one tense weekend and wants to cancel afterward; the annual tier works out to about 77¢ per week if you keep it. Both include unlimited scans, all four scan modes, all 25+ pest entries, the DIY methods library, expert chat, and the exterminator finder. There is no separate per-scan fee.

How do I cancel my PestSnap subscription?

On your iPhone, open Settings, tap your name at the top, tap Subscriptions, find PestSnap, and tap Cancel Subscription. The cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period — the app continues working until then. To avoid being charged after the trial, cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends. If you cancel within the trial, you are not charged.

Does PestSnap work offline?

The bug identification itself requires an internet connection because the AI vision model runs on a server, not on your iPhone. The DIY methods library, the emergency phone numbers (Poison Control, Pet Poison Helpline), and previously-completed scans are available offline. If you are scanning in a basement with poor signal, take the photo first — when signal returns, PestSnap finishes the identification.

Does PestSnap recommend specific products?

Yes, when one product clearly outperforms alternatives for a given pest at a given budget tier. For example, for German cockroaches the app recommends specific gel bait brands because they substantially outperform sprays for that species. Some product links are affiliate links — we disclose this in the app's About section under Affiliate Disclosure and on every recommendation card. The recommendation algorithm prioritizes effectiveness for the identified pest, not commission rate.

Can I use PestSnap outside the US?

You can install and run it from anywhere the App Store is available, and many of the pests it covers (cockroaches, bed bugs, fleas, ticks, mosquitoes, common spiders) are global. But PestSnap's pest catalog, DIY product recommendations, exterminator finder, and the emergency phone numbers (Poison Control, Pet Poison Helpline) are US-centric. If you are in Canada, the UK, or Australia, the bug ID will usually work, but the next-step recommendations may not match your local product availability. Localizations for en-GB, DE, and FR are on the roadmap.

Will PestSnap identify a brown recluse or black widow?

It tries to, and is conservative about it. The two medically significant US spiders — brown recluse (Loxosceles reclusa) and black widow (Latrodectus mactans) — are both in the database. When the app sees a candidate, it returns the identification at a confidence level and recommends an in-person identification by a professional exterminator before any action that requires touching the spider. Misidentifying a wolf spider as a brown recluse is common because of similar coloration; the markings the app looks for (violin-shaped marking, eye arrangement) are not always visible in normal phone photos. If you have any reason to believe you have been bitten by either, call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) regardless of what the app says.

What if PestSnap identifies an infestation?

For infestation-risk verdicts (termites, bed bugs, German cockroaches, fire ants, carpenter ants) the app does not push DIY-only solutions. It offers a path: the DIY methods if you want to try first, and a one-tap exterminator finder that connects you to licensed pros in your area with quotes in minutes. The exterminator finder is a referral integration with services like Terminix, Orkin, and Ehrlich — we disclose any affiliate relationship in the app's About section. Confirmed termite or large-scale bed bug infestations almost always need a professional; we say so plainly.

Can I trust the DIY product recommendations?

For the 25+ pests in the catalog, the DIY methods are reviewed against published academic and university extension service sources (Cornell IPM, UC IPM, USDA, EPA pesticide guidance) plus the manufacturer-claimed efficacy of recommended products. Where the academic evidence is mixed (essential-oil sprays, ultrasonic repellers), we say so rather than promising results. The library is updated quarterly. For health-sensitive situations — pregnancy, infants in the home, pets, chemical sensitivities — we link to non-chemical methods first.

Does PestSnap replace calling 911 for a severe reaction?

No. PestSnap is an identification reference, not a medical service. For severe allergic reactions (difficulty breathing, throat swelling, widespread hives), suspected severe spider envenomation, or any bite where the affected person is going into shock — call 911 immediately. Do not stop to take a photo. PestSnap has Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) and Pet Poison Helpline (1-855-764-7661) one tap from the home screen for exactly the case where you do need to identify something quickly but you also need professional medical guidance.

Who builds PestSnap?

PestSnap is built by Loveiko Labs, an iOS studio founded in 2024. The studio publishes around a dozen single-purpose AI apps including JewelSnap, WatchSnap, VeriBag, and BumpCheck. PestSnap is funded by user subscriptions and affiliate revenue from disclosed exterminator referrals — there are no advertisers, no banner ads, and no data sales.

Editorial · 2026 Ranking

# Best Pest Identifier Apps in 2026 — Honest Ranking

Seven AI bug identifier apps for iPhone, compared by what they actually do — not by which one shouts loudest in App Store screenshots.

 See the ranking

Overview

## There is no single best app — there is a best app for each job

The first thing to know: there is no single best pest identifier app. There is a best app for each of three different jobs — homeowner pest verdict, naturalist learning, and free citizen science — and we say which is which.

Disclosure: we make PestSnap, ranked #1 in this list for home pest identification. Picture Insect and Seek are objectively better for the larger naturalist audience. We tried to write this the way we would want a competitor to write it about us.

We compared seven apps that are currently active in the US App Store and have at least 50 reviews. The ranking weighs five factors:

- Coverage and accuracy for the apps' stated identification scope.

- Audience fit — is the app actually built for the people who need it most?

- Next-step utility — does it just name the bug, or does it help you do something with that information?

- Pricing and value — what does the user pay and what do they get?

- Trust signals — track record, transparency about limitations, honest disclaimers.

The Ranking

## Best pest identifier apps 2026 — ranked

01

### PestSnap (Loveiko Labs — us) — best for home pests, bites, and pet parasites

This is the app we build, so we are biased. We placed it first in this list for home pest identification — but for naturalist learning and free use, Picture Insect and Seek genuinely beat us, and we are not trying to displace them. PestSnap is built for a narrower job neither of those apps does well: the homeowner who needs a verdict on what to do about a bug in the house, the renter staring at three bites in a line on her arm, the parent identifying what bit her kid, the dog owner picking a tick off after a hike.

Strengths. Four scan modes (Bug / Bite / Evidence / Pet) instead of just one. Plain-English verdict (harmless / nuisance / infestation risk). 3–5 specific DIY methods per pest. One-tap exterminator finder. Emergency phone access (Poison Control, Pet Poison Helpline). Built specifically for the 25+ US home pests most people actually encounter. 7-day free trial — longer than competitors.

Weaknesses. New app (released 2026) with smaller install base than Picture Insect. Narrower catalog — if you want to identify a butterfly in the garden, this is not the app. No free tier (subscription-only after 7-day trial). US-centric — international users get bug IDs but DIY product recommendations and emergency numbers do not localize yet.

Pick PestSnap if you are dealing with a pest in your home, on your skin, or on your dog and you want a verdict plus next-step recommendations.

02

### Picture Insect by Glority — best for naturalists

Picture Insect is the most-installed bug identifier on the App Store, and for good reason. Glority has been refining it since 2019 across multiple identifier apps (PlantSnap, PictureBird, PictureFish), and the entomology database is the deepest in the consumer market — 10,000+ species globally with naturalist-style entries covering habitat, life cycle, geographic range, and behavior.

Strengths. Largest database. Most mature app. Strong gallery and sharing features. Decent free tier for occasional use. Excellent for kids learning bug names.

Weaknesses. Built for naturalist curiosity rather than homeowner problem-solving. Returns Latin species names and encyclopedia entries; does not return "harmless / nuisance / infestation risk" verdicts. No bite identification. No droppings/evidence mode. No pet parasite mode. No DIY pest control methods. No exterminator finder.

Pick Picture Insect if you want to know what a beautiful longhorn beetle is. Pick something else if you want to know what to do about the roach in your kitchen.

### Seek by iNaturalist — best free option for families

Seek is the kid-friendly version of iNaturalist, made by the same nonprofit. Real-time camera identification (no need to even take a photo), gamified achievement system, fully free with no ads or premium tier. It covers plants, animals, and insects — not just bugs.

Strengths. Fully free. No login required for basic use. Privacy-friendly (no data collection). Excellent for families with kids who want to explore the backyard. Identification quality is genuinely good — backed by iNaturalist's community-trained models.

Weaknesses. Focused on outdoor wildlife rather than indoor pests. Will identify a wolf spider but not tell you whether it is dangerous in your kitchen. No bite identification, no evidence mode, no actionable next steps. The community-trained model has gaps for very common indoor pests (German cockroach, bedbug).

Pick Seek if you have kids who want to identify bugs in the park, and you do not want to pay anything.

04

### iNaturalist — best for citizen scientists

iNaturalist is the grown-up version of Seek. Same nonprofit, same database, but designed for serious naturalists and researchers — every identification you log contributes to a global biodiversity database used by ecologists, conservation organizations, and universities. The identification accuracy is comparable to Seek, but the app expects engagement (login, community participation, identification verification).

Strengths. Fully free. Massive scientifically-validated database. Community of millions of naturalists who can confirm or correct your identifications. Open data — contributions are publicly accessible and used in real research.

Weaknesses. Not optimized for "what bit me at 2 a.m." moments. The community-confirmation workflow adds friction. Less polished UX than Picture Insect or PestSnap. No DIY methods, no exterminator finder, no consumer pest framing.

Pick iNaturalist if you want to contribute to actual biodiversity science while learning bug ID. Pick something else if you need a quick consumer answer.

It does basic photo-to-species identification reasonably well and packages results in a naturalist-style encyclopedia entry. Does not differentiate meaningfully from Insect Identifier or InsectSnap on features.

Pick it if you have tried Picture Insect's free tier and want a paid alternative at a similar price point — but most users end up going back to Picture Insect or Seek after the trial.

Pick it if you are a curious explorer who wants occasional bug IDs and the other options in this tier are unavailable in your region.

How we judged

## Methodology — pick by scenario, not by ranking

The ranking above reflects the primary job each app was built for. Here is how the same apps map to specific situations:

 | Your situation | Best app | Why

 | "Kid found a beautiful bug in the park" | Seek (free) or Picture Insect | Naturalist coverage, gamified for kids, free option available

 | "What is this bug crawling on my kitchen counter?" | PestSnap | Plain-English verdict, DIY methods, infestation risk assessment

 | "I woke up with three bites in a row on my arm" | PestSnap | Only app with Scan the Bite mode that analyzes bite patterns

 | "What is this strange caterpillar in my garden?" | Picture Insect | Best naturalist database, life cycle info, host plant info

 | "There are droppings near the kitchen — what is it?" | PestSnap | Only app with Scan the Evidence mode for droppings, mud tubes, etc.

 | "There is a tick on my dog after our hike" | PestSnap | Scan on Pet mode plus direct Pet Poison Helpline access

 | "I want to identify bugs and contribute to science" | iNaturalist | Real biodiversity database, community-verified IDs

 | "I want a free bug ID app for occasional use" | Seek (totally free) | No subscription, no ads, no login required

 | "I think I see termites in the basement" | PestSnap, then a licensed exterminator | App gives verdict, but termites need professional confirmation

We compared all seven apps that are currently active in the US App Store and have at least 50 reviews. The ranking weighs coverage and accuracy for each app's stated scope, audience fit, next-step utility, pricing and value, and trust signals including track record and transparency about limitations.

### When no app is enough

All seven apps above are AI-vision identification tools. None of them are medical, veterinary, or professional pest control services. Situations where you should put the app down:

- Severe bite reaction — difficulty breathing, throat swelling, hives, rapid spreading, fever, bullseye rash. Call 911 or Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).

- Confirmed infestation — termites, bed bugs at scale, German cockroaches established in a kitchen. Call a licensed exterminator.

- Pet bitten by a tick in a Lyme-endemic region with attachment over 24 hours — call your vet or Pet Poison Helpline (1-855-764-7661).

- Brown recluse or black widow bite with symptoms — Poison Control immediately, regardless of any app's verdict.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Which pest identifier app has the largest bug database?

Picture Insect by Glority has the largest consumer database — 10,000+ species globally with naturalist-style entries covering habitat, life cycle, geographic range, and behavior. iNaturalist's community-verified database is also vast and scientifically rigorous. PestSnap intentionally has a narrower catalog focused on the 25+ pests most commonly encountered in US homes, which makes it more actionable for homeowners but less useful for naturalists wanting to identify exotic or garden species.

Is there a completely free pest identifier app?

Yes — Seek by iNaturalist is fully free with no subscription, no ads, and no login required. iNaturalist is also fully free. Picture Insect has a limited free tier that allows a handful of identifications per day. PestSnap, Bug Identifier, Insect Identifier, and InsectSnap are all subscription apps that offer free trials (PestSnap's 7-day trial is longer than the 3-day trials offered by the others).

Which app is best for identifying a bug bite on skin?

PestSnap is the only app in this ranking with a dedicated Bite scan mode. You photograph the bite pattern, and the app analyzes the spacing, shape, and arrangement to suggest what insect likely caused it. No other app in this ranking offers bite identification — Picture Insect, Seek, and iNaturalist are focused on identifying live insects from photos, not bite marks on skin.

Can any of these apps identify droppings or pest evidence?

PestSnap is the only app with a Scan the Evidence mode that lets you photograph droppings, mud tubes, shed skins, or damage patterns. The other six apps require a photo of the insect itself to make an identification.

Which app is best for families with young children?

Seek by iNaturalist. It requires no login, has no data collection, features a gamified achievement system that kids enjoy, and uses real-time camera identification. It is free and covers plants and animals broadly — not just insects. iNaturalist is the more serious version of the same platform for older teens and adults who want to contribute to science.

How does PestSnap compare to Picture Insect on price?

Picture Insect costs approximately $29.99 per year (with a limited free tier). PestSnap costs $39.99 per year or $4.99 per week, with a 7-day free trial. For the naturalist use case, Picture Insect's annual plan offers more breadth. For home pest identification with DIY guidance, PestSnap's extra features justify the modest price difference.

## Dealing with a pest at home? PestSnap has you covered.

# RoofingCalc Pro — the roofing calculator that works on the roof

Four calculators in one free app: roof area and materials, pitch, rafter length and job cost. Punch in measurements, get squares, bundles, rafter lengths and a job price, then export a clean one-page PDF for the client or the claim file — fully offline, with big tap targets for gloved hands. No ads, no subscription, no account.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone & iPad · iOS 17.6+ · 100% free · works offline · zero data collected

Overview

## What is RoofingCalc Pro?

RoofingCalc Pro is a professional roofing calculator for roofers, contractors, estimators, insurance adjusters, apprentices and DIY homeowners who need fast, correct roofing math on the job site — even with no signal.

Roofing math is not hard, but it is easy to get wrong on a ladder in the sun: converting footprint to sloped area, area to squares, squares to bundles, run and pitch to rafter length, and all of it to a price with waste. RoofingCalc Pro does those conversions instantly and keeps every calculation in history.

It is deliberately simple: no aerial measurement subscriptions, no per-report fees, no CRM. You bring the measurements; it gives you the numbers and a PDF. Everything runs locally on the device — it works on the roof, in rural areas, anywhere.

Completely free. Every feature is included — no hidden costs, no premium tier, no ads, no popups. RoofingCalc Pro collects zero data: no account, no analytics.

Audience

## Who RoofingCalc Pro is built for

### Professional roofers

Area, materials and rafter lengths on every job; PDF estimates from the truck.

### General contractors

Quick, reliable roofing math when roofing isn't your primary trade.

### Insurance adjusters

Roof area and replacement cost for storm-damage claims, with a PDF for the file.

### Roofing apprentices

Learn the formulas — slope factor, hip/valley factor — while getting accurate answers.

### DIY homeowners

Estimate materials before calling contractors, so you can read their quotes with confidence.

### Anyone without signal

Everything runs on the device. No internet, no problem.

Capabilities

## Four calculators, one free app

- Roof area & materials. Enter footprint dimensions and pitch. Get roof area in square feet and in roofing squares (1 square = 100 sq ft), plus shingle bundles, underlayment rolls and ridge cap pieces.

- Pitch calculator. Enter rise and run to get pitch as a ratio (e.g. 6/12), in degrees and as a percentage — or enter any one value and calculate the others. Slope factor and hip/valley factor are shown for your own calculations.

- Rafter length. Enter run and pitch to get common, hip and valley rafter lengths using the correct geometric factors. Cut lumber right the first time.

- Job cost estimator. Enter roof area, material cost per square, labor rate and waste factor for a full breakdown: materials, labor, waste allowance and total job price.

- PDF export. A professional one-page report with all calculations — send it to the client, adjuster or office from the job site.

- History, units and job-site UI. Every calculation saved automatically and searchable by date or project. Imperial or metric with one tap. High-contrast green-on-dark theme readable in bright sun; big tap targets for gloves.

Workflow

## How to estimate a re-roof in five steps

A typical re-roof estimate with RoofingCalc Pro, from tape measure to PDF.

- Measure the footprint and pitch.Measure the building footprint including overhangs, and get the pitch — rise over a 12-inch run. If you only have degrees or percent, the pitch calculator converts it.

- Calculate area and squares.Enter dimensions and pitch in Roof Area & Materials. You get sloped area in square feet and roofing squares. Example: a 2,000 sq ft footprint at 6/12 pitch (slope factor ≈ 1.118) is about 2,236 sq ft, or ≈ 22.4 squares.

- Get materials.Read off shingle bundles, underlayment rolls and ridge cap. Standard 3-tab and many architectural shingles run three bundles per square — check the manufacturer's coverage for the product you use.

- Price the job.In the Job Cost Estimator, enter material cost per square, labor rate and a waste factor (commonly around 10% for simple gables and more for complex hip roofs with valleys). You get materials, labor, waste and total.

- Export the PDF.Generate the one-page report and send it to the client or adjuster. The calculation stays in history for when the client calls back.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Is RoofingCalc Pro really free?

Yes. Every feature is included — no hidden costs, no per-report charges, no premium tier, no ads and no popups.

Does it work without internet?

Yes. All calculations run locally on your device, so it works on the roof, in rural areas and anywhere without signal.

How many squares is my roof?

One roofing square is 100 square feet of roof surface. Multiply the footprint area by the slope factor for your pitch to get sloped area, then divide by 100. RoofingCalc Pro does this for you from footprint dimensions and pitch.

How many bundles of shingles per square?

Many standard 3-tab and architectural shingles need three bundles per square, but coverage varies by product — always check the manufacturer's label. RoofingCalc Pro calculates bundles, underlayment rolls and ridge cap from your roof area.

How do I convert roof pitch to degrees?

Pitch is rise over a 12-inch run. Degrees = arctangent(rise ÷ 12). For example, 6/12 ≈ 26.6°, 4/12 ≈ 18.4°, 12/12 = 45°. The pitch calculator converts between ratio, degrees and percentage in either direction.

Can it calculate hip and valley rafters?

Yes. Enter run and pitch to get common, hip and valley rafter lengths using the correct slope and hip/valley factors.

Can I send an estimate to a client?

Yes. Export a professional one-page PDF with all calculations and send it from the job site.

Does it measure my roof from satellite images?

No. RoofingCalc Pro is a calculator — you enter the measurements. For aerial measurement, services like GAF QuickMeasure or EagleView sell reports.

What data does RoofingCalc Pro collect?

None. No account, no analytics, no ads. Your calculations stay on your device.

Is it safe to measure a roof myself?

Roof work is dangerous. Use proper fall protection and never go on a wet, icy or steep roof without training and equipment. Measuring from the ground or from plans is often safer for homeowners.

## How we ranked these apps

"Roofing app" covers three different jobs: calculators that turn your measurements into squares, materials and prices; measurement services that measure the roof for you from aerial imagery; and sales and business platforms. This ranking puts them side by side so you can pick the right tool — or the right two.

Across 7 apps we evaluated the features that matter to an actual user, not the ones that look good on a landing page:

- Core math. Area, squares, pitch conversions and rafter lengths.

- Materials and pricing. Bundles, underlayment, ridge cap, waste, labor and total job cost.

- Measurement. Does the app measure the roof for you, or do you bring the numbers?

- Job-site usability. Offline, readable in sunlight, usable with gloves.

- Output. PDF estimates, reports or blueprints.

- Cost. Free, paid per report, or subscription.

Roof work is dangerous — use fall protection. Calculators give estimates; verify against manufacturer specs and local code.

How do I calculate roofing squares?

Sloped roof area ÷ 100. Sloped area = footprint × slope factor (≈ 1.054 at 4/12, 1.118 at 6/12, 1.202 at 8/12, 1.414 at 12/12).

Overview

## What is ColorCheck?

ColorCheck is an iPhone AI shopping guard that determines your precise 12-season color profile and then gives you a live BUY or SKIP verdict on any clothing item — in 3 seconds, in any store.

The problem it solves: 20–30% of every closet in America was never worn (ThredUp data). 49% of women report fitting-room frustration tied to color decisions (Zalando/YouGov study, 14,609 respondents). The financial cost averages $1,500 per year. The dominant cause is not style — it is color. Wrong-undertone clothing makes your skin look sallow or ruddy. Wrong-depth clothing washes you out. Wrong-contrast clothing overwhelms your features. You typically cannot tell which is happening under store lighting (warm halogen, fluorescent, LED — all biased). ColorCheck is the 3-second diagnostic that closes that gap before you commit money.

- In-store BUY or SKIP verdict — the core job. Point your camera at any clothing item. Three seconds. ## How a ColorCheck session works — four steps

- Take 3 photos for your color season.Selfie in natural daylight (window light, no filter, no makeup if possible). Close-up of your eyes. Close-up of your wrist (showing veins for undertone). Total time: under 2 minutes.

A 32-year-old Warm Autumn user audits 60 items in her closet. Result: 36 KEEP, 24 Donate-or-Resell. Original purchase value of the donate pile: $1,840. Expected Poshmark resale: $370–550. Most painful finding: $280 of items still had tags. After the audit she eliminated cool pinks, powder blues, lavenders, pure whites, and pure blacks from future purchases. Eight months later: $1,200 lifetime savings counter, closet feels coordinated, "nothing to wear" feeling essentially disappeared.

### The online return cycle breaker

You return 24–40% of what you order from ASOS — often because "the color in the photo wasn't the real color." You screenshot the product page and run it through ColorCheck. The scanner corrects for ASOS's known neutral-bias filter and gives you a verdict on what color the item probably actually is. Your return rate drops from 38% to under 10% over the next two months.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

How is ColorCheck different from other color analysis apps?

Every other color analysis app gives you an abstract palette and stops there. ColorCheck is the only app that gives you a BUY or SKIP verdict on the specific clothing item you're holding in the store. The palette is the entry point, not the product. After determining your color season from a 3-photo analysis, you point your camera at any garment and get a 3-second verdict — Olive Green 87% match BUY, or Mint Green 23% match SKIP with a suggested warmer alternative.

How accurate is the color season determination?

ColorCheck uses 3 photos in different lighting (selfie + close-up of eyes + wrist) and averages the results. A test of 23 people showed standard AI color analysis apps return correct results only 26% of the time when single-photo and binary. Multi-photo averaging plus confidence scoring addresses both failure modes. If your confidence score is below 70%, ColorCheck explicitly recommends a re-analysis with better lighting rather than committing to an uncertain season.

What's the 12-season color analysis system?

The 12-season system is the professional color analysis standard used by certified colorists worldwide. It extends the basic 4 seasons (Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter) into 3 variations each:
- Spring: Light Spring, True Spring, Bright Spring
- Summer: Light Summer, True Summer, Soft Summer
- Autumn: Soft Autumn, True Autumn, Deep Autumn
- Winter: Cool Winter, True Winter, Deep Winter
It captures variation in undertone (warm/cool), contrast level (high/medium/low), and depth (light/medium/deep). Same framework professional stylists use in $200–800 consultations.

Why do I get different seasons from different apps?

Three reasons:
- Single-photo apps are sensitive to lighting variation — a selfie in cool indoor light reads "cool" colors; the same person in warm window light reads "warm." Multi-photo averaging (ColorCheck's approach) fixes this.
- Binary verdicts with no confidence score hide uncertainty. If you're truly on the boundary between Soft Autumn and Soft Summer, different apps will land on different sides. ColorCheck's confidence score makes this visible.
- Training data differences — many apps trained primarily on light-skinned subjects perform poorly on darker skin tones. ColorCheck's training set covers all Fitzpatrick types.

What if my confidence score is low?

If confidence is below 70%, ColorCheck explicitly says so and recommends re-analysis. Common causes:
- Photos taken in mixed lighting (window + indoor lamp)
- Heavy makeup that masks your natural undertone
- Hair color that doesn't match your natural color
- Photos with strong filters or skin smoothing
Retake in natural daylight (window light, no direct sun), no makeup, hair tied back. The repeat analysis is free and unlimited during your Pro subscription.

How does the BUY or SKIP verdict work?

The scanner does three things:
- Identifies the specific shade of the garment (e.g. "Warm Olive Green")
- Compares it against your personal color palette to compute a match score (0–100%)
- Returns the verdict with a one-sentence explanation
80%+ match = BUY IT. 40–79% = neutral, your call (it won't hurt you but isn't optimal). Under 40% = SKIP IT with a suggested alternative in your palette.

Does ColorCheck work in any store lighting?

Yes, but accuracy improves in better lighting. Store lighting is typically biased — fitting rooms use warm halogen, fluorescent under-light, or fluorescent overhead. ColorCheck's scanner is calibrated to correct for common store lighting types. For best results in particularly bad lighting (very yellow incandescent, very blue LED), step closer to a window or store entrance.

Can ColorCheck scan online product photos?

Yes via screenshot. The Phase 2 feature corrects for known store filter biases — Anthropologie photos are noticeably warm/sepia, ASOS leans neutral, Zara varies. The scanner adjusts for the known filter pattern of each major retailer. For unfamiliar retailers, the scanner uses general color correction but flags lower confidence on the verdict.

What about patterned or multi-color clothing?

For multi-color patterns, the scanner identifies the dominant color and gives a verdict on that. For complex patterns (florals, prints), it gives an "overall harmony score" — how well the combination of colors aligns with your palette. Generally: solid colors give the most reliable verdicts. Two-tone patterns work well. Complex prints are best evaluated by considering the dominant color individually.

How does the savings counter work?

Every time you scan an item in a store and get a SKIP verdict, the item's price tag value is added to your monthly savings counter. Home screen shows totals like "Saved $341 this month" based on actual purchases avoided. Most users find their savings exceed the annual subscription cost within the first 2–3 weeks. The counter creates visible ROI — wellness-tracking apps show streaks, ColorCheck shows dollars.

Will ColorCheck work for men, dark skin tones, or specific eye colors?

Yes. The 12-season color analysis system works across all skin tones, hair colors, and eye colors. Training data covers Fitzpatrick skin types I through VI. For darker skin tones specifically, the system relies more on undertone (warm/cool) and contrast level (high/medium/low) than on absolute skin color — the correct methodology used by professional colorists. The dominant user base is currently women aged 25–45, but the system is gender-neutral and works for all genders.

What if I don't like my color season?

This is more common than people expect — particularly with Soft Autumn (muted earthy palette) and Light Summer (very desaturated palette). Two things to remember:
- Every season has rich and beautiful shades. Soft Autumn includes the deep rust of fall leaves, mossy greens, rich olives, warm taupes. The "muted" framing is misleading.
- Match score is a spectrum, not binary. 60% match doesn't mean "you can't wear this" — it means "decent, not ideal."
The celebrity color twin feature helps here — when Jessica Alba is your example, "Warm Autumn" stops feeling drab and starts feeling like a real aesthetic.

Should I use ColorCheck if I've already paid a stylist for color analysis?

Yes — but for a different job. The stylist gave you a palette (the entry point). ColorCheck's value is the in-store BUY/SKIP scanner for individual items, which no stylist can give you when you're standing in Zara at 7 PM. Many ColorCheck users already know their season; they use the app for the scanner only.

Does ColorCheck handle vintage or thrift store finds?

Yes — vintage and thrift items are a common use case. The shade identification works on any clothing item regardless of where it came from. ColorCheck pairs well with SnapFlip for thrift store flipping — SnapFlip handles the resale price lookup and Flip Score, ColorCheck handles the personal-fit verdict.

What does the closet audit feature do exactly?

Scan items already in your closet. Each gets a KEEP or DONATE verdict. The final report shows:
- Count of items in your palette (KEEP)
- Count of items outside your palette (DONATE candidates)
- Estimated dollars tied up in wrong-color clothing
- Resale value if you sell on Poshmark or ThredUp
Most users scan 10–30 items the first day. Positive framing: "These 7 items are PERFECT for you" rather than "Donate these 5." Generates the value moment that justifies the subscription before the trial ends.

How much does ColorCheck cost?

Free to download with a 7-day free trial including full Pro access. No quiz before paywall, no email gate, clear close button on the subscription screen. After trial:
- Weekly: $4.99/week
- Annual: $39.99/year (saves 85% vs weekly)
Compare to a professional color analysis session: $200–800 with a stylist. ColorCheck Pro for an entire year costs less than the cheapest professional session — and you get the in-store BUY/SKIP scanner, which no stylist can give you in real time.

Why is the trial 7 days instead of 3?

Industry data (RevenueCat 2026): 7-day trials have approximately 40.4% conversion rate vs 25.5% for 3-day trials. Three days isn't enough time for most users to actually go shopping and try the scanner in a real store. By Day 5 of a 7-day trial, most users have used it at least once on an actual purchase decision — generating the proof moment. ColorCheck deliberately uses 7 days because the trial needs to span at least one shopping event for the app to prove its value.

How do I cancel ColorCheck Pro?

All subscriptions are managed through Apple. To cancel:
- Open Settings
- Tap your Apple ID
- Tap Subscriptions
- Find ColorCheck → tap Cancel Subscription
Takes effect at the end of the current billing period. The 7-day trial can be cancelled any time before it ends with no charge — no questions asked, no dark patterns.

Does my data stay private?

Yes. Selfie photos used for color analysis are processed on-device when possible and stored locally to your iPhone — not uploaded to ColorCheck servers unless you explicitly choose iCloud sync. Anonymous color season metadata may be used to improve the AI model. Photos are never shared with third parties, used for advertising, or sold.

Is ColorCheck affiliated with Zara, Anthropologie, or any retailer?

No. ColorCheck is an independent iOS app developed by Loveiko Labs, an iOS app studio. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or partnered with any clothing retailer, brand, or e-commerce platform.

Eighteen-plus color analysis apps exist on the App Store. This ranking weights the BUY/SKIP in-store scanner, multi-photo averaging for stable results, and honest paywalls above all other criteria.

Overview

## What we measured — and why

Most color analysis apps share the same problem: they identify your season, hand you an abstract palette, and stop there. The harder challenge — deciding whether the specific olive blouse you're holding in Zara matches your palette — goes unsolved across most of the category.

This ranking weights the features that affect real purchase decisions, not just seasonal categorisation. Full disclosure: we make ColorCheck, ranked first. We've tried to be honest about where competitors win.

- In-store decision support (35%) — BUY/SKIP scanner for individual items, not just abstract palettes

- Color season accuracy (25%) — multi-photo averaging, confidence scoring, training across all skin tones

- Paywall honesty (15%) — quiz-free onboarding, transparent pricing, clear cancellation

- Feature depth (15%) — savings counter, closet audit, AI stylist, PDF report

- User satisfaction signals (10%) — rating, recent sentiment, update cadence

## Methodology

We tested each app with the same set of criteria applied to a consistent set of use cases: initial season determination, in-store item scanning, paywall transparency, and result consistency.

### Non-app alternatives

Quick context on what the category competes against:

- Professional color stylist ($200–800): The gold standard for accuracy. Downside: high cost, 4–8 week waiting list, doesn't help you in stores after the session. ColorCheck Pro for a full year costs less than one stylist session.

- Korean color studios (House of Colour, Klook listings, $50–300 + travel): Excellent accuracy. Requires being in Seoul. Niche option.

- DIY draping kit ($30–50 on Amazon): Physical fabric swatches you hold up to your face. Time-intensive (1–2 hours), subjective, no fit verdict on actual garments.

- Color Me Beautiful swatch fan ($30–50): Gives you the colors but doesn't tell you BUY or SKIP on a specific item. Common complaint: "I was handed this tiny 3x8 swatch card... and now what?"

- ChatGPT or Claude with image upload (free to $20/month): Decent quality on a single photo but takes 5+ minutes per scan, no memory between sessions, no savings tracking. Not optimised for in-store speed.

- r/coloranalysis on Reddit (free): Crowdsourced opinions. Commenters frequently disagree. Hours to days for a verdict. Useful for a second opinion, not for in-store decisions.

### The recommendation

For most color analysis users in 2026:

- Use ColorCheck for the BUY/SKIP scannerBest for in-store decisions and online item verification.

- Optionally pair with Style DNAIf you specifically want extensive outfit recommendations and lookbooks.

- Skip apps with documented paywall trap behaviorPalette specifically — regardless of how good the underlying tech might be.

Download ColorCheck for the 7-day free trial. Take the color analysis. Scan 10–20 items in your closet for the audit. If it identifies wrong-color items you didn't know about, the value is proven. If not, cancel before the trial ends with one tap.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

What makes ColorCheck different from other color analysis apps?

ColorCheck is the only consumer color analysis app with an in-store BUY/SKIP scanner — point your camera at any garment and get a 3-second verdict on whether it matches your palette. It also uses multi-photo averaging (3 photos) for stable season determination, and a savings counter that shows the dollar amount saved on avoided wrong-color purchases. No other app in the category combines all three features.

Is Style DNA better than ColorCheck?

It depends on what you need. Style DNA is better for styling content — outfit lookbooks, virtual try-on, and fashion recommendations. ColorCheck is better for decision support on specific items: the BUY/SKIP scanner, multi-photo averaging for accurate season detection, and the savings counter. If you want a "fashion assistant," Style DNA wins. If you want to know whether the blouse you're holding in a store matches your palette, ColorCheck wins.

Which color analysis app has the most accurate results?

Accuracy is hard to measure objectively, but result consistency is measurable. WhatColors has documented reports of giving 6 different results from 6 scans of the same person. Dressika similarly produces inconsistent results across different photos. ColorCheck uses 3-photo averaging to produce a stable result — users report the same season result across multiple separate test sessions. ColorMine claims 95%+ accuracy across 30,000 sessions, but has too few App Store reviews to verify at scale.

Is there a color analysis app with no subscription?

Yes — My Best Colors offers $14.99 lifetime pricing, which is unusual in the category. The trade-off is basic feature depth: it identifies your color season and the color of items you scan, but doesn't give a BUY/SKIP verdict, has no savings counter, and doesn't offer multi-photo averaging. Good value if you specifically want a one-time purchase with no recurring cost.

What is a "paywall trap" in color analysis apps?

A paywall trap is an onboarding pattern where an app presents a subscription screen with no obvious close button — users report feeling forced to pay or aggressively close the app to proceed. Palette is the most-cited example in the color analysis category, with multiple reviews using language like "You're trapped there." ColorCheck was designed specifically to avoid this: the subscription screen has a visible close button, and a 7-day full-Pro trial starts without requiring payment information upfront.

How do I cancel a color analysis app subscription?

All App Store subscriptions (ColorCheck, Style DNA, Dressika, Palette, and others) are managed through Apple's subscription system. Go to Settings → your Apple ID → Subscriptions, find the app, and tap Cancel Subscription. You retain access until the end of the billing period you've already paid for. You do not need to contact the app developer to cancel.

iOS App · Mind & Faith · Salah & Quran

# Sakinah — understand the words of your salah

You've said these words thousands of times. Sakinah explains the salah you already know by heart — Al-Fatiha, the words of the prayer and the short surahs — one phrase at a time, in the order you pray.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone · iOS 17.0+ · 7-day free trial on Weekly · 8 languages · no ads, no account

Overview

## What is Sakinah?

Sakinah is an iPhone app that explains the meaning of the salah you already pray: Al-Fatiha, the words of the prayer and 15 short surahs, one phrase at a time, in the order you pray. Each phrase comes with the Arabic text, its meaning and a simple explanation, plus prayer times and the qibla.

Many Muslims learned the prayer as children, by sound, and recite it every day without knowing what each phrase means. Sakinah is built for that gap. It doesn't ask you to start over — it starts from the words you already say.

The rhythm is small: one phrase before a prayer, one short question after. A few minutes, at your pace. There are no tests and no streaks, and you can begin with whichever part of the prayer interests you.

What Sakinah does not do. It explains the meaning of the words. It does not judge your prayer or your pronunciation and does not give fatwas. For practice, follow your teacher and your community.

Audience

## Who Sakinah is for

### You pray, but don't speak Arabic

You know Al-Fatiha and the tashahhud by heart. Sakinah shows you what each phrase means, so the words you recite become words you understand.

### You want to start small

One phrase before a prayer and one short question after. No tests, no streaks — just a few minutes when you have them.

### Parents teaching children

"Words for my child" shows how to explain a phrase to your kids, and a kids' version offers phrases made simple and selected cartoons about prayer.

### Families on one plan

One subscription covers the family through Family Sharing, so parents and children can each use the app on their own devices.

### People who want prayer times without clutter

Prayer times for your city are calculated on your phone, with the qibla on a compass or through your camera. No ads, no account — and these stay free if your plan ends.

### Anyone with questions about a word

Ask the Sakinah guide about a word or phrase from your lessons and see what the answer is based on. Save the phrases that matter to you in My words, with your own notes.

Capabilities

## What Sakinah includes

- Al-Fatiha, verse by verse. Each verse of Al-Fatiha, and Āmīn, with the Arabic text, its meaning and a simple explanation.

- The words of the prayer. Takbir, ruku, sujud, tashahhud, salawat, taslim, the opening supplication and seeking refuge — the phrases you say in every rak'ah, explained in the order you pray them.

- 15 short surahs. Surahs you can recite after Al-Fatiha, including Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas, Al-Kawthar and Al-Asr.

- Recitation with word highlighting. Quran verses recited by Mishary Rashid Alafasy, with each word highlighted as it is read, so you can follow the Arabic while you listen.

- Prayer times and qibla. Prayer times for your city, calculated on your phone: your country's method, standard or Hanafi Asr, or your own mosque's times. The qibla direction on a compass, or shown on the floor through your camera.

- A phrase to take into your prayer. A reminder with your phrase before you pray, and a gentle "did you catch it?" afterwards. Your salah appears as a map of words, so you can see what you already understand.

- Sakinah guide (AI). Ask about any word or phrase from your lessons. The guide answers and shows what the answer is based on. It explains meanings — it does not issue rulings.

- For the whole family. "Words for my child", a kids' version, My words with your own notes, today's phrase as a Home Screen widget, and Family Sharing. No ads, no account.

Workflow

## How Sakinah works — your first week, one phrase at a time

The free week is designed as a gentle routine you can keep, not a course to finish.

- Day 1 — pick where to start.Open Al-Fatiha, the words of the prayer or a short surah — whichever interests you. You get full access, with nothing to pay today.

- Before a prayer — read one phrase.See the Arabic text, its meaning and a simple explanation. Listen to the recitation and follow the highlighted words. A reminder brings your phrase to you before you pray.

- After the prayer — one short question.A gentle "did you catch it?" asks whether you noticed the phrase as you prayed. It isn't a test, and there is no streak to protect.

- Along the way — ask and save.Ask the Sakinah guide about a word, save phrases to My words with your own notes, and use "Words for my child" if you want to share a phrase with your kids.

- Day 7 — decide.The weekly plan starts on day 7 unless you cancel in Settings at least 24 hours before. Cancel in time and you pay nothing. Prayer times and the qibla stay free either way.

In practice

## Situations where Sakinah helps

Illustrative examples of how the features fit into a day — not user reviews.

### Before Fajr, one phrase

You open the reminder before the morning prayer and read one verse of Al-Fatiha with its meaning. After you pray, Sakinah asks whether you caught it. Over the week, your map of words starts to fill in.

### The surah you always choose

You usually recite Al-Ikhlas after Al-Fatiha. You open it in Sakinah, listen to the recitation with each word highlighted, and read what each phrase means.

### A question from your child

Your child asks what they are saying in the tashahhud. "Words for my child" shows a way to explain the phrase simply, and the kids' version gives them phrases of their own.

### A word you want to understand better

You ask the Sakinah guide about a word from your lesson. It answers and shows what the answer is based on. You save the phrase to My words with a note. For anything about how to pray, you ask your teacher.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

What is Sakinah?

Sakinah is an iPhone app that explains the meaning of the salah you already pray: Al-Fatiha, the words of the prayer and 15 short surahs, one phrase at a time, in the order you pray. Every phrase comes with the Arabic text, its meaning and a simple explanation.

Does Sakinah check my pronunciation or tell me if my prayer is correct?

No. Sakinah explains the meaning of the words. It does not judge your prayer or your pronunciation and does not give fatwas. For questions of practice, follow your teacher and your community.

Which parts of the prayer does Sakinah cover?

Al-Fatiha verse by verse, and Amin; the words of the prayer, including takbir, ruku, sujud, tashahhud, salawat, taslim, the opening supplication and seeking refuge; and 15 short surahs you can recite after Al-Fatiha, such as Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas, Al-Kawthar and Al-Asr.

Is Sakinah a full Quran app?

No. Sakinah focuses on what you recite in salah: Al-Fatiha, the words of the prayer and 15 short surahs. If you want to read the whole Quran with translations and many reciters, a dedicated Quran app such as Quran by Quran.com is the better tool, and many people use both.

Whose recitation is used in the app?

Quran verses are recited by Mishary Rashid Alafasy, and each word is highlighted as it is read, so you can follow the Arabic while you listen.

What does the Sakinah guide (AI) do?

The Sakinah guide answers your questions about a word or a phrase from your lessons and shows what the answer is based on. It explains meanings; it is not a scholar and does not give religious rulings.

Can I use Sakinah with my children?

Yes. There is a kids' version with phrases made simple and selected cartoons about prayer, and a feature called Words for my child that shows how to explain a phrase to your kids. One subscription covers your family through Family Sharing.

How does the free week work?

New subscribers on the weekly plan get 7 days free with full access and nothing to pay on the first day. On day 7 the weekly plan starts unless you cancel in Settings at least 24 hours before. If you cancel in time, you pay nothing.

How much does Sakinah cost?

In the US, Sakinah Plus is $7.99 per week after a 7-day free trial for new subscribers, or $39.99 per year with no free trial. Family Sharing is included. Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period.

What stays free if my plan ends?

Prayer times and the qibla direction stay free if your plan ends.

How are prayer times calculated?

Prayer times for your city are calculated on your phone. You can use your country's method, choose standard or Hanafi Asr, or enter your own mosque's times.

Do I need an account, and are there ads?

No account is needed and there are no ads. Sakinah is available in Arabic, English, French, German, Indonesian, Malay, Russian and Turkish.

About religious guidance. Sakinah explains the meaning of the words of the prayer. It does not judge your prayer or your pronunciation and does not give fatwas or religious rulings. For questions of practice — how to pray, what to recite, matters of fiqh — follow your teacher and your community.

About the AI guide. The Sakinah guide answers questions about words and phrases from your lessons and shows what its answer is based on. Like any AI, it can be incomplete or wrong; treat it as a study aid, not a scholar.

About prayer times. Prayer times are calculated on your phone from the method you choose. If your local mosque follows different times, you can enter your mosque's times instead.

Editorial · 2026 Guide · Last updated October 2026

# Best Quran & Prayer Apps 2026 — to understand your salah

Five iPhone apps for the Quran, prayer times and the words of the prayer — compared honestly, including our own with full disclosure.

 See the list

Last updated October 2026 · ratings checked on the US App Store at time of writing

Overview

## How we chose these apps

Most Muslim apps answer one of three questions: when to pray, which way to face, and what the Quran says. Fewer help with a quieter question many people carry for years — what do the words I say in every prayer actually mean? This guide covers five iPhone apps worth installing in 2026 and who each one is really for.

We looked at what matters in daily use, not what looks good on a store page:

- Understanding the prayer. Does the app explain the meaning of what you recite in salah, or only the text?

- Quran depth. The full mushaf with translations and reciters, or a focused set of surahs?

- Prayer times and qibla. Calculation methods, Asr options and whether you can use your mosque's times.

- Learning the movements. Step-by-step guidance for beginners, converts and children.

- Calm by design. Ads, accounts, streaks and pressure — or the absence of them.

- Price and track record. What is free, what is paid, and how many ratings the app has.

None of these apps replaces a teacher, an imam or your community. App descriptions below are summarized from each app's public App Store listing at time of writing, October 2026.

The List

## 5 Quran & prayer apps for iPhone in 2026

01

### Sakinah — Best for Understanding the Words of Your Salah (Our App, Full Disclosure)

Disclosure. Sakinah is built by Loveiko Labs — the studio publishing this article. We list it first for one specific need: understanding what you say in prayer. If you want the full Quran or a long track record, see #2 and #3.

What it is. An app that explains the salah you already know by heart — Al-Fatiha verse by verse, the words of the prayer (takbir, ruku, sujud, tashahhud, salawat, taslim, the opening supplication and seeking refuge) and 15 short surahs — one phrase at a time, in the order you pray. Each phrase has the Arabic text, its meaning and a simple explanation, with recitation by Mishary Rashid Alafasy and each word highlighted as it is read.

Best for. People who pray daily but don't speak Arabic; parents who want to explain the prayer to their children.

Strengths. One phrase before a prayer, one short question after — no tests, no streaks. Prayer times calculated on your phone (country method, standard or Hanafi Asr, or your mosque's times) and a qibla on a compass or through the camera. An AI guide for questions about words from your lessons that shows what its answer is based on. Kids' version, Family Sharing, no ads, no account. Prayer times and qibla stay free if your plan ends.

Limitations. Released October 2026 — no App Store ratings yet. Not a full Quran app. Explains words, not movements. Subscription: $7.99/week after a 7-day free trial, or $39.99/year. It does not judge your prayer or pronunciation and does not give fatwas.

Sakinah overview on Loveiko Labs

02

### Quran by Quran.com — Best Free Full Quran

What it is. A free, ad-free mushaf app from Quran Foundation, Inc. for reading, memorizing and listening to the Quran, with translations including The Clear Quran by Dr. Mustafa Khattab, multiple reciters and several mushaf layouts.

Best for. Anyone who wants to read or listen to the whole Quran with translations, without ads or a subscription.

Strengths. 4.9★ from about 33K ratings at time of writing, October 2026. Free and ad-free. Adjustable playback speed, verse looping, bookmarks and notes. Open source.

Limitations. A Quran app, not a prayer app — prayer times and qibla are not listed. It does not walk you through the words of salah in prayer order.

Quran by Quran.com on the App Store

03

### Muslim Pro — Best All-in-One Muslim App

What it is. A large all-in-one app from Bitsmedia Pte Ltd: prayer times and Athan notifications, the full Quran with recitations and translations, qibla, Hijri calendar, duas and dhikr with a tasbih counter, a prayer and fasting tracker, and a halal restaurant and prayer space finder.

Best for. People who want one app for nearly every daily Islamic need, backed by a very large user base.

Strengths. 4.7★ from about 600K ratings at time of writing, October 2026. Broad feature set and many interface languages.

Limitations. Free to download, but many features sit behind paid tiers, and an ad-removal purchase is offered. A breadth-first app — a phrase-by-phrase explanation of the words of salah is not listed. Streaks and gamified quests may not suit everyone.

Muslim Pro on the App Store

04

### Pillars — Best Ad-Free Prayer Times & Qibla

What it is. A prayer times and qibla app from The Pillars Group Ltd with multiple calculation methods, early or late Asr, a calibrated qibla finder, prayer and fasting trackers, and Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets.

Best for. People who want clean prayer times and qibla without ads or clutter.

Strengths. 4.8★ from 5.6K+ ratings at time of writing, October 2026. No ads, a privacy-focused design and VoiceOver accessibility. Free to download.

Limitations. Focused on prayer times — Quran reading and explanations of the words of salah are not listed. Some features, such as Apple Watch support, are part of Pillars Premium (from $11.99/month).

Pillars: Prayer Times & Qibla on the App Store

05

### Salah 3D — Best for Learning the Movements of the Prayer

What it is. A step-by-step prayer guide with 3D animation of each position, wudu guidance, audio of the Arabic passages when you tap the words, transliteration and English translations, covering the five daily prayers.

Best for. Beginners, converts and children learning how to pray, and anyone refreshing their practice.

Strengths. Shows the movements visually, which none of the other apps here focus on. Low one-time price: free to download, with the full guide as a $2.99 in-app purchase.

Limitations. 4.2★ from 21 ratings at time of writing, October 2026 — a small review base. Prayer times, qibla and the full Quran are not listed. As with any how-to-pray app, details can differ between schools; check with your teacher.

Salah 3D: Namaz Prayer Guide on the App Store

How we judged

## Which app fits your situation

An honest guide does not put the publisher's app first without saying why. Here is where each app genuinely wins — including the cases where ours is not the right pick. Ratings and review counts were checked on the US App Store in October 2026.

 | Your situation | Best pick

 | You pray daily and want to understand the words you say | Sakinah — phrase by phrase, in prayer order

 | You want the full Quran with translations, free | Quran.com

 | You want one app for prayer times, Quran, duas and more | Muslim Pro

 | You want ad-free prayer times and qibla | Pillars, or Sakinah (free if your plan ends)

 | You are learning how to pray, step by step | Salah 3D, alongside a teacher

 | You want to explain the prayer to your children | Sakinah — "Words for my child" and a kids' version

 | Track record matters most | Muslim Pro or Quran.com

 | You want to pay nothing at all | Quran.com

### What none of these apps do

None of these apps — including ours — replaces a teacher, an imam or your community. Sakinah states plainly that it explains the meaning of the words and does not judge your prayer or your pronunciation, and does not give fatwas.

Calculated prayer times depend on the method you choose. If your local mosque follows different times, follow your mosque; some apps, including Sakinah, let you enter your mosque's times.

Many people use two apps: one for the full Quran, and one for prayer times or for understanding the prayer. That is a perfectly good setup.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Why is your own app listed first?

Sakinah is the only app in this list built around explaining the meaning of the words you recite in salah, phrase by phrase, in the order you pray. It is also the newest app here, released in October 2026 with no ratings yet, and it is not a full Quran app. If you want the full Quran or a long track record, Quran.com and Muslim Pro are the stronger picks.

What is the best free Quran app?

Quran by Quran.com is free and ad-free according to its App Store listing, with translations and multiple reciters. Muslim Pro and Pillars are free to download with paid upgrades.

Which app helps me understand the meaning of my prayer?

Sakinah explains Al-Fatiha, the words of the prayer and 15 short surahs one phrase at a time, with the Arabic text, its meaning and a simple explanation. Salah 3D includes English translations and transliteration inside its step-by-step guide.

Which app is best for learning how to pray step by step?

Salah 3D is built for that: a step-by-step guide with 3D animation of the prayer and wudu guidance, aimed at beginners, converts and children. Sakinah explains the words, not the movements. For the details of practice, learn from a teacher in your community.

Can a prayer app tell me if my prayer or recitation is correct?

None of the apps in this guide claims to judge whether your prayer is valid. Sakinah states clearly that it does not judge your prayer or pronunciation and does not give fatwas. For practice and rulings, follow your teacher and your community.

Which app is best for prayer times without ads?

Pillars describes itself as ad-free and privacy-focused, with multiple calculation methods and early or late Asr. Sakinah also has no ads and calculates prayer times on your phone, and its prayer times and qibla stay free if your plan ends.

iOS App · Mind · Affirmations

# Herself — hear your moment already going well

Your inner critic has had the mic long enough. Answer a few questions, read aloud for 15 seconds, and listen to a one-minute scene where your moment has already gone well — read by an AI voice made from your recording.

 Download on the App Store
 See how it works

iPhone · iOS 17.0+ · 7-day free trial on Weekly · 18 languages · adults 18+

Overview

## What is Herself?

Herself is an iPhone app that turns what you want into a one-minute audio scene where your moment has already gone well, read by an AI voice made from a 15-second recording of your own voice. It is a self-practice tool for calm and confidence — not therapy, not medical care, and it doesn't promise results.

Most affirmation apps hand you a sentence someone else wrote. Herself starts with you: what you want — to believe in yourself, love, calm about money, a new job, a home of your own — and a line in your own words. From that it builds a short scene you can play in the morning, before the big conversation, or at night.

The scene is read in a voice made from yours. Before each chapter you read a fresh 15 seconds aloud; the recording is deleted right after the voice copy is made, and the voice copy is deleted within an hour after your scene.

What makes it different: instead of a library of generic lines, you get chapters — the first right away, the second on day 4, then a new one every week, built from what changed for you. Your line of the day sits on your Lock Screen and Home Screen widget, and a 20-second version of your own lines plays on repeat for right before the hard moment.

Audience

## Who Herself is built for

### Wanting to believe in yourself

If the loudest voice in your head is the critical one, Herself gives you a minute of hearing a different version — your moment going well, in a voice that sounds like yours.

### Before a big conversation

Play your scene before the talk you've been putting off, or use the 20-second version of your own lines on repeat right before you walk in.

### Looking for a new job

Tell Herself it's about work, add a line in your own words, and listen to your scene in the morning before applications or an interview.

### Wanting calm about money

Money worry can be constant background noise. A one-minute scene at night is a small, deliberate pause from it.

### Love and a home of your own

Personal hopes — love, a place that's yours — are the kind of thing Herself is built around. You choose the goal; the scene is written from your answers.

### Adults who want something short

Herself is for adults 18+. Each scene is about a minute, and your line of the day lives on a widget, so the practice fits into a normal day.

Capabilities

## What Herself gives you

- A one-minute scene of your moment going well. Built from a few taps and a line in your own words, then read aloud so you can listen rather than read.

- An AI voice made from yours. Read a short text aloud for 15 seconds and your scene is read in a voice copy made from that recording. The voice copy only ever reads your own scenes.

- Chapters that keep coming. Your first chapter right away, the second on day 4, then a new chapter every week, built from what changed for you.

- Line of the day on your widget. Your line of the day appears on your Lock Screen and Home Screen widget.

- A 20-second version on repeat. A short version of your own lines, looping, for right before the hard moment.

- Edit the words. Change any sentence of your scene for free, and re-voice it once within an hour.

- Extra chapters if you want them. Want more than one a week? Extra chapters are one-time purchases while your plan is active, and they never expire.

- Your voice stays yours. A fresh 15-second recording before each chapter, deleted right after the voice copy is made; the voice copy deleted within an hour after your scene. Scenes stay on your iPhone, and you can delete them and withdraw consent anytime in Settings.

Workflow

## How Herself works — three steps, then chapters over time

The setup takes a few taps. After that, the practice is listening.

- Tell Herself what you want.To believe in yourself, love, calm about money, a new job, a home of your own. A few taps and a line in your own words.

- Read a short text aloud for 15 seconds.This recording is used to make a voice copy, and it is deleted right after the voice copy is made.

- Listen to your one-minute scene.Your moment going well, in an AI voice made from yours. Play it in the morning, before the big conversation, or at night.

- Adjust it if a line doesn't sound like you.Change any sentence for free, and re-voice it once within an hour. The voice copy is deleted within an hour after your scene.

- Keep going with new chapters.The second chapter arrives on day 4, then a new one every week, built from what changed for you. You read a fresh 15 seconds before each chapter.

Comparison

An honest side-by-side based on each app's public App Store listing at time of writing, October 2026. Herself is new and takes a different approach: one personal scene instead of many short lines.
